passages.original: After dinner, my sleepiness return'd, and being shown to a bed, I lay down without undressing, and slept till six in the evening, was call'd to supper, went to bed again very early, and slept soundly till next morning. Then I made myself as tidy as I could, and went to Andrew Bradford the printer's. I found in the shop the old man his father, whom I had seen at New York, and who, travelling on horseback, had got to Philadelphia before me. He introduc'd me to his son, who receiv'd me civilly, gave me a breakfast, but told me he did not at present want a hand, being lately suppli'd with one; but there was another printer in town, lately set up, one Keimer, who, perhaps, might employ me; if not, I should be welcome to lodge at his house, and he would give me a little work to do now and then till fuller business should offer.
passages.vernacular: 食完飯,我又眼瞓,被帶去一張床,我冇脫衫就瞓低,一直瞓到晚上六點,被叫去食晚餐,然後好早又去瞓,一覺瞓到第二朝。然後我盡量整理得整齊,去咗印刷商安德魯·布拉德福德嗰度。我喺舖頭見到佢老爸,即係我喺紐約見過嗰位老先生;佢騎馬旅行,比我早到費城。佢將我介紹畀佢個仔,佢禮貌咁接待我,請我食早餐,但話而家暫時唔需要人手,因為最近剛請咗一個;不過鎮上有另一個新開嘅印刷商,叫凱默,或者會請我;如果唔得,歡迎我住喺佢屋企,佢會不時畀啲少少工作我做,直到有更多生意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吃完飯,我又睏了,被帶到一張床,我沒脫衣服就躺下,一直睡到晚上六點,被叫去吃晚飯,然後很早又去睡,一覺睡到第二天早上。然後我盡量整理得整齊,去了印刷商安德魯·布拉德福德那裡。我在店裡見到他父親,就是我在紐約見過的那位老先生;他騎馬旅行,比我早到費城。他把我介紹給他兒子,他禮貌地接待我,請我吃早餐,但說現在暫時不需要人手,因為最近剛請了一個;不過鎮上有另一個新開的印刷商,叫凱默,或許會僱我;如果不行,歡迎我住在他家,他會不時給我一點工作做,直到有更多生意。

passages.original: The old gentleman said he would go with me to the new printer; and when we found him, "Neighbor," says Bradford, "I have brought to see you a young man of your business; perhaps you may want such a one." He ask'd me a few questions, put a composing stick in my hand to see how I work'd, and then said he would employ me soon, though he had just then nothing for me to do; and, taking old Bradford, whom he had never seen before, to be one of the town's people that had a good will for him, enter'd into a conversation on his present undertaking and prospects; while Bradford, not discovering that he was the other printer's father, on Keimer's saying he expected soon to get the greatest part of the business into his own hands, drew him on by artful questions, and starting little doubts, to explain all his views, what interests he reli'd on, and in what manner he intended to proceed. I, who stood by and heard all, saw immediately that one of them was a crafty old sophister, and the other a mere novice. Bradford left me with Keimer, who was greatly surpris'd when I told him who the old man was.
passages.vernacular: 老先生話會陪我去見嗰個新印刷商;我哋搵到佢之後,布拉德福德講:「街坊,我帶咗一個同你同行嘅後生嚟睇你;或者你需要呢種人。」佢問咗我幾個問題,放一支排字架喺我手,睇我點做嘢,然後話好快會請我,雖然而家暫時冇嘢畀我做;佢以為布拉德福德老先生(佢從未見過)係鎮上一個對佢有善意嘅人,就同佢傾起自己當前嘅事業同前景;而布拉德福德冇透露自己係另一個印刷商嘅爸爸,凱默講自己預期好快將大部分生意拉入自己手上,佢就用巧妙嘅問題同小小嘅質疑,引佢講出所有打算,倚靠咩利益,同打算點樣進行。我企喺旁邊,全部聽到,即刻睇出其中一個係狡猾嘅老詭辯家,另一個只係新手。布拉德福德將我留喺凱默度走咗;我話畀凱默聽嗰位老先生係邊個,佢非常驚訝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老先生說會陪我去見那個新印刷商;我們找到他之後,布拉德福德說:「鄰居,我帶了一個和你同行的年輕人來看你;也許你需要這種人。」他問了我幾個問題,把一支排字架放在我手裡,看我怎麼做,然後說很快會僱我,雖然現在暫時沒有東西給我做;他以為布拉德福德老先生(他從未見過)是鎮上一個對他有善意的人,就和他談起自己當前的事業和前景;而布拉德福德沒有透露自己是另一個印刷商的父親,凱默說自己預期很快把大部分生意拉到自己手上,他就用巧妙的問題和小小的質疑,引他講出所有打算,倚靠什麼利益,以及打算怎樣進行。我站在旁邊,全部聽到,立刻看出其中一個是狡猾的老詭辯家,另一個只是新手。布拉德福德把我留在凱默那裡走了;我告訴凱默那位老先生是誰,他非常驚訝。

passages.original: Keimer's printing-house, I found, consisted of an old shatter'd press, and one small, worn-out font of English which he was then using himself, composing an Elegy on Aquila Rose, before mentioned, an ingenious young man, of excellent character, much respected in the town, clerk of the Assembly, and a pretty poet. Keimer made verses too, but very indifferently. He could not be said to write them, for his manner was to compose them in the types directly out of his head. So there being no copy, but one pair of cases, and the Elegy likely to require all the letter, no one could help him. I endeavor'd to put his press (which he had not yet us'd, and of which he understood nothing) into order fit to be work'd with; and, promising to come and print off his Elegy as soon as he should have got it ready, I return'd to Bradford's, who gave me a little job to do for the present, and there I lodged and dieted. A few days after, Keimer sent for me to print off the Elegy. And now he had got another pair of cases, and a pamphlet to reprint, on which he set me to work.
passages.vernacular: 我發現凱默嘅印刷所,淨係有一部破爛舊印刷機,同一小套用舊咗嘅英文鉛字;佢當時自己正用緊,排緊一首輓歌,悼念前面提過嘅阿奎拉·羅斯,一個聰明嘅後生,品格優良,好受鎮上嘅人尊敬,係議會書記,又係個相當好嘅詩人。凱默都作詩,不過好差。其實不能話佢「寫」,因為佢嘅方式係直接用鉛字由腦袋裡面排出嚟。所以冇底稿,只有一對字盤,而輓歌又好似要用晒所有鉛字,冇人幫到佢。我努力將佢嘅印刷機(佢未用過,又全不了解)整理到可以操作;答應佢一準備好輓歌就嚟印,然後返去布拉德福德度,佢暫時畀咗個小工作我做,我就喺嗰度住同食。幾日後,凱默叫我去印輓歌。而家佢有另一對字盤,同一本要重印嘅小冊子,佢叫我做呢個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我發現凱默的印刷所,只有一部破爛舊印刷機,和一小套用舊了的英文鉛字;他當時自己正在用,排著一首輓歌,悼念前面提過的阿奎拉·羅斯,一個聰明的年輕人,品格優良,很受鎮上的人尊敬,是議會書記,又是個相當好的詩人。凱默也作詩,不過很差。其實不能說他「寫」,因為他的方式是直接用鉛字從腦子裡排出來。所以沒有底稿,只有一對字盤,而輓歌又似乎要用完所有鉛字,沒有人幫得了他。我努力把他的印刷機(他還沒用過,又完全不了解)整理到可以操作;答應他一準備好輓歌就來印,然後回到布拉德福德那裡,他暫時給了我一個小工作,我就在那裡住和吃。幾天後,凱默叫我去印輓歌。現在他有另一對字盤,和一本要重印的小冊子,他叫我做這個。

passages.original: These two printers I found poorly qualified for their business. Bradford had not been bred to it, and was very illiterate; and Keimer, tho' something of a scholar, was a mere compositor, knowing nothing of presswork. He had been one of the French prophets, and could act their enthusiastic agitations. At this time he did not profess any particular religion, but something of all on occasion; was very ignorant of the world, and had, as I afterward found, a good deal of the knave in his composition. He did not like my lodging at Bradford's while I work'd with him. He had a house, indeed, but without furniture, so he could not lodge me; but he got me a lodging at Mr. Read's, before mentioned, who was the owner of his house; and, my chest and clothes being come by this time, I made rather a more respectable appearance in the eyes of Miss Read than I had done when she first happen'd to see me eating my roll in the street.
passages.vernacular: 我發現呢兩個印刷商都唔太勝任自己嘅行業。布拉德福德並冇受過呢行訓練,好冇學問;凱默雖然有啲學問,但只係個排字工人,對印刷工作一竅不通。佢曾經係「法國先知」之一,能夠模仿佢哋狂熱嘅激動。佢當時冇宣稱任何特定宗教,但有需要時又有各教少少;對世情好無知,而我後來發現,佢性格當中有相當成分嘅奸詐。我同佢做嘢嘅時候,佢唔鍾意我住喺布拉德福德度。佢確實有間屋,但冇傢俬,所以冇辦法畀我住;但佢幫我喺前面提過嘅里德先生度搵到住處,里德係佢屋嘅業主;我嘅箱同衫到咗之後,我喺里德小姐眼中,比起佢第一次碰巧見到我喺街上食麵包卷嗰陣,顯得體面咗少少。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我發現這兩個印刷商都不太勝任自己的行業。布拉德福德並沒受過這一行的訓練,沒什麼學問;凱默雖然有些學問,但只是個排字工人,對印刷工作一竅不通。他曾經是「法國先知」之一,能夠模仿他們狂熱的激動。他當時沒宣稱任何特定宗教,但有需要時又各教都沾一點;對世情很無知,而我後來發現,他性格當中有相當成分的奸詐。我和他做事的時候,他不喜歡我住在布拉德福德那裡。他確實有間屋,但沒傢俱,所以沒辦法給我住;但他幫我在前面提過的里德先生那裡找到住處,里德是他屋子的業主;我的箱子和衣服到了之後,我在里德小姐眼中,比起她第一次碰巧見到我在街上吃麵包卷時,顯得體面了一些。

passages.original: I began now to have some acquaintance among the young people of the town, that were lovers of reading, with whom I spent my evenings very pleasantly; and gaining money by my industry and frugality, I lived very agreeably, forgetting Boston as much as I could, and not desiring that any there should know where I resided, except my friend Collins, who was in my secret, and kept it when I wrote to him. At length, an incident happened that sent me back again much sooner than I had intended. I had a brother-in-law, Robert Holmes, master of a sloop that traded between Boston and Delaware. He being at Newcastle, forty miles below Philadelphia, heard there of me, and wrote me a letter mentioning the concern of my friends in Boston at my abrupt departure, assuring me of their good will to me, and that every thing would be accommodated to my mind if I would return, to which he exhorted me very earnestly. I wrote an answer to his letter, thank'd him for his advice, but stated my reasons for quitting Boston fully and in such a light as to convince him I was not so wrong as he had apprehended.
passages.vernacular: 我開始認識鎮上幾個愛讀書嘅後生,同佢哋度過好愉快嘅晚上;我靠勤奮同節儉賺錢,生活好愜意,盡量忘記波士頓,亦唔想嗰度任何人知道我住喺邊,只有我朋友柯林斯知道我嘅秘密,而我寫信畀佢,佢都有守秘。終於發生一件事,令我比預計快好多返去。我有個姐夫羅伯特·霍姆斯,係一艘喺波士頓同德拉瓦之間做貿易嘅單桅帆船嘅船長。佢當時喺費城下游四十英里嘅紐卡斯爾,聽到我嘅消息,就寫咗封信畀我,講我波士頓嘅親友對我突然離開好擔心,保證佢哋對我有善意,如果我返去,一切都會按我心意安排,佢非常誠懇咁勸我返去。我回信,多謝佢嘅意見,但詳細講明我離開波士頓嘅理由,而且講得令佢相信我冇佢擔心嗰麼錯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我開始認識鎮上幾個愛讀書的年輕人,和他們度過非常愉快的夜晚;我靠勤奮和節儉賺錢,生活很愜意,盡量忘記波士頓,也不想那裡任何人知道我住在哪裡,只有我朋友柯林斯知道我的秘密,而我寫信給他,他也有守秘。終於發生了一件事,使我比預計早得多回去。我有個姐夫羅伯特·霍姆斯,是一艘在波士頓和德拉瓦之間做貿易的單桅帆船的船長。他當時在費城下游四十英里的紐卡斯爾,聽到我的消息,就寫了封信給我,說我在波士頓的親友對我突然離開很擔心,保證他們對我有善意,如果我回去,一切都會按我的心意安排,他非常誠懇地勸我回去。我回了信,感謝他的意見,但詳細說明我離開波士頓的理由,而且說得使他相信我沒有他擔心的那麼錯。

passages.original: Sir William Keith, governor of the province, was then at Newcastle, and Captain Holmes, happening to be in company with him when my letter came to hand, spoke to him of me, and show'd him the letter. The governor read it, and seem'd surpris'd when he was told my age. He said I appear'd a young man of promising parts, and therefore should be encouraged; the printers at Philadelphia were wretched ones; and, if I would set up there, he made no doubt I should succeed; for his part, he would procure me the public business, and do me every other service in his power. This my brother-in-law afterwards told me in Boston, but I knew as yet nothing of it; when, one day, Keimer and I being at work together near the window, we saw the governor and another gentleman (which proved to be Colonel French, of Newcastle), finely dress'd, come directly across the street to our house, and heard them at the door.
passages.vernacular: 威廉·基思爵士,即省督,當時喺紐卡斯爾;我嘅信到達時,霍姆斯船長碰巧同佢喺一齊,就同佢講起我,拎我嘅信畀佢睇。省督睇完,聽到我嘅年紀之後似乎好驚訝。佢話我似乎係個有前途嘅後生,所以應該得到鼓勵;費城嘅印刷商都好差;如果我肯喺嗰度開業,佢毫不懷疑我會成功;至於佢,會幫我爭取公家生意,並盡佢所能提供其他一切幫助。呢件事我姐夫後來喺波士頓話畀我聽,但我當時一無所知;有一日,凱默同我喺窗邊一齊做嘢,見到省督同另一位紳士(原來係紐卡斯爾嘅弗倫奇上校),衣著華麗,直接橫過街嚟我哋屋,又聽到佢哋喺門口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 威廉·基思爵士,即省督,當時在紐卡斯爾;我的信到達時,霍姆斯船長碰巧和他在一起,就跟他談起我,拿我的信給他看。省督看完,聽到我的年紀之後似乎很驚訝。他說我似乎是個有前途的年輕人,所以應該得到鼓勵;費城的印刷商都很差;如果我肯在那裡開業,他毫不懷疑我會成功;至於他,會幫我爭取公家生意,並盡他所能提供其他一切幫助。這件事我姐夫後來在波士頓告訴我,但我當時一無所知;有一天,凱默和我在窗邊一起做事,看見省督和另一位紳士(原來是紐卡斯爾的弗倫奇上校),衣著華麗,直接橫過街來我們屋子,又聽到他們在門口。

passages.original: Keimer ran down immediately, thinking it a visit to him; but the governor inquir'd for me, came up, and with a condescension of politeness I had been quite unus'd to, made me many compliments, desired to be acquainted with me, blam'd me kindly for not having made myself known to him when I first came to the place, and would have me away with him to the tavern, where he was going with Colonel French to taste, as he said, some excellent Madeira. I was not a little surprised, and Keimer star'd like a pig poison'd. I went, however, with the governor and Colonel French to a tavern, at the corner of Third-street, and over the Madeira he propos'd my setting up my business, laid before me the probabilities of success, and both he and Colonel French assur'd me I should have their interest and influence in procuring the public business of both governments. On my doubting whether my father would assist me in it, Sir William said he would give me a letter to him, in which he would state the advantages, and he did not doubt of prevailing with him. So it was concluded I should return to Boston in the first vessel, with the governor's letter recommending me to my father. In the mean time the intention was to be kept a secret, and I went on working with Keimer as usual, the governor sending for me now and then to dine with him, a very great honor I thought it, and conversing with me in the most affable, familiar, and friendly manner imaginable.
passages.vernacular: 凱默即刻跑落去,以為係嚟探佢;但省督問起我,上到嚟,以一種我完全唔慣嘅禮貌謙遜,對我說咗好多讚美嘅話,想認識我,溫和咁責怪我第一次嚟呢度時冇令佢知道,又要我同佢一齊去酒館,佢同弗倫奇上校要去嗰度品嚐,佢話,一啲好嘅馬德拉酒。我好驚訝,而凱默瞪大眼,好似隻中咗毒嘅豬。不過我還是同省督同弗倫奇上校去咗第三街轉角嘅酒館,飲住馬德拉酒,佢提議我開業,向我分析成功嘅可能性,佢同弗倫奇上校都向我保證,我會得到佢哋嘅利益同影響力,爭取兩個政府嘅公家生意。我懷疑我爸爸會唔會幫我,威廉爵士話會寫封信畀佢,講明好處,毫不懷疑可以說服佢。於是決定我乘第一艘船返波士頓,帶住省督推薦我嘅信畀我爸爸。同時,呢個打算要保密;我照常同凱默做嘢,省督不時叫我去同佢食飯,我覺得係極大嘅榮譽,而且用最親切、熟絡、友善嘅方式同我傾偈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 凱默立刻跑下去,以為是來探他;但省督問起我,上來了,以一種我完全不習慣的禮貌謙遜,對我說了許多讚美的話,想認識我,溫和地責怪我第一次來這裡時沒讓他知道,又要我跟他一起去酒館,他和弗倫奇上校要去那裡品嚐,他說,一些好的馬德拉酒。我很驚訝,而凱默瞪大眼,像隻中了毒的豬。不過我還是跟省督和弗倫奇上校去了第三街轉角的酒館,喝著馬德拉酒,他提議我開業,向我分析成功的可能性,他和弗倫奇上校都向我保證,我會得到他們的利益和影響力,爭取兩個政府的公家生意。我懷疑我父親會不會幫我,威廉爵士說會寫封信給他,說明好處,毫不懷疑可以說服他。於是決定我乘第一艘船回波士頓,帶著省督推薦我的信給我父親。同時,這個打算要保密;我照常跟凱默做事,省督不時叫我去跟他吃飯,我覺得是極大的榮譽,而且用最親切、熟絡、友善的方式和我交談。

passages.original: About the end of April, 1724, a little vessel offer'd for Boston. I took leave of Keimer as going to see my friends. The governor gave me an ample letter, saying many flattering things of me to my father, and strongly recommending the project of my setting up at Philadelphia as a thing that must make my fortune. We struck on a shoal in going down the bay, and sprung a leak; we had a blustering time at sea, and were oblig'd to pump almost continually, at which I took my turn. We arriv'd safe, however, at Boston in about a fortnight. I had been absent seven months, and my friends had heard nothing of me; for my br. Holmes was not yet return'd, and had not written about me. My unexpected appearance surpriz'd the family; all were, however, very glad to see me, and made me welcome, except my brother. I went to see him at his printing-house. I was better dress'd than ever while in his service, having a genteel new suit from head to foot, a watch, and my pockets lin'd with near five pounds sterling in silver. He receiv'd me not very frankly, look'd me all over, and turn'd to his work again.
passages.vernacular: 1724年4月底,有一艘小船去波士頓。我同凱默告辭,話去探親友。省督畀咗封詳盡嘅信我,對我爸爸講咗好多讚美我嘅話,強烈推薦我喺費城開業嘅計劃,話必定令我發達。我哋沿海灣落去嘅時候擱淺,船漏水;喺海上風浪好大,幾乎要不停抽水,我都輪流做。不過大約兩個星期後,我哋平安抵達波士頓。我離開咗七個月,我親友對我全無消息;因為我姐夫霍姆斯仲未返嚟,亦冇寫信講我。我突然出現令家人驚訝;不過所有人都好高興見到我,歡迎我,除咗我哥哥。我去佢印刷所探佢。我穿得比喺佢手下做嘢時好得多,由頭到腳一套體面嘅新衫,有隻錶,袋裡面有近五英鎊銀幣。佢接待我不太坦率,上下打量我一番,就轉返去做嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 1724年4月底,有一艘小船去波士頓。我向凱默告辭,說去探親友。省督給了封詳盡的信給我,對我父親說了許多讚美我的話,強烈推薦我在費城開業的計劃,說必定使我發達。我們沿海灣下去的時候擱淺,船漏水;在海上風浪很大,幾乎要不停抽水,我也輪流做。不過大約兩個星期後,我們平安抵達波士頓。我離開了七個月,我的親友對我全無消息;因為我姐夫霍姆斯還沒回來,也沒寫信說我。我突然出現令家人驚訝;不過所有人都很高興見到我,歡迎我,除了我哥哥。我去他的印刷所探他。我穿得比在他手下做事時好得多,從頭到腳一套體面的新衣,有隻錶,口袋裡有近五英鎊銀幣。他接待我不太坦率,上下打量我一番,就轉回去做事。

passages.original: The journeymen were inquisitive where I had been, what sort of a country it was, and how I lik'd it. I prais'd it much, the happy life I led in it, expressing strongly my intention of returning to it; and, one of them asking what kind of money we had there, I produc'd a handful of silver, and spread it before them, which was a kind of raree-show they had not been us'd to, paper being the money of Boston. Then I took an opportunity of letting them see my watch; and, lastly (my brother still grum and sullen), I gave them a piece of eight to drink, and took my leave. This visit of mine offended him extreamly; for, when my mother some time after spoke to him of a reconciliation, and of her wishes to see us on good terms together, and that we might live for the future as brothers, he said I had insulted him in such a manner before his people that he could never forget or forgive it. In this, however, he was mistaken.
passages.vernacular: 工人好奇我去咗邊、嗰邊係個點樣嘅地方、我鍾唔鍾意。我大讚嗰度,講我喺嗰度過嘅快樂生活,強烈表示打算返去;其中一個問嗰度用咩錢,我攞出一把銀幣攤開喺佢哋面前,對佢哋嚟講好似睇西洋鏡,因為波士頓用紙幣。然後我藉機畀佢哋睇我隻錶;最後(我哥哥仍然陰沉不語),我畀咗佢哋一個西班牙銀元去飲酒,就告辭。我呢次探訪極度冒犯咗佢;因為過咗一段時間,我媽媽同佢講和解,話希望見到我哋和好,以後做兄弟生活,佢話我喺佢手下人面前咁侮辱佢,佢永遠不能忘記或原諒。不過喺呢點上,佢錯咗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 工人們好奇我去了哪裡、那邊是個怎樣的地方、我喜不喜歡。我大讚那裡,講我在那裡過的快樂生活,強烈表示打算回去;其中一個問那裡用什麼錢,我拿出一把銀幣攤開在他們面前,對他們來說好像看西洋鏡,因為波士頓用紙幣。然後我藉機給他們看我的錶;最後(我哥哥仍然陰沉不語),我給了他們一個西班牙銀元去喝酒,就告辭。我這次探訪極度冒犯了他;因為過了一段時間,我母親跟他談和解,說希望見到我們和好,以後做兄弟生活,他說我在他手下人面前那樣侮辱他,他永遠不能忘記或原諒。不過在這一點上,他錯了。

passages.original: My father received the governor's letter with some apparent surprise, but said little of it to me for some days, when Capt. Holmes returning he showed it to him, ask'd him if he knew Keith, and what kind of man he was; adding his opinion that he must be of small discretion to think of setting a boy up in business who wanted yet three years of being at man's estate. Holmes said what he could in favor of the project, but my father was clear in the impropriety of it, and at last gave a flat denial to it. Then he wrote a civil letter to Sir William, thanking him for the patronage he had so kindly offered me, but declining to assist me as yet in setting up, I being, in his opinion, too young to be trusted with the management of a business so important, and for which the preparation must be so expensive.
passages.vernacular: 我爸爸收到省督嘅信,似乎有啲驚訝,但幾日冇同我講乜;霍姆斯船長返嚟之後,佢拎畀佢睇,問佢識唔識基思,佢係咩樣嘅人;又補充話,佢認為此人一定好缺乏判斷力,居然諗到幫一個距離成年仲差三年嘅男孩開業。霍姆斯盡佢所能講咗啲贊成計劃嘅話,但我爸爸明確認為不適當,最後斷然拒絕。然後佢寫咗封客氣嘅信畀威廉爵士,多謝佢好意提供贊助,但婉拒暫時幫我開業,因為佢認為我太年輕,唔夠資格被託付管理一項咁重要、準備又必須咁昂貴嘅生意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我父親收到省督的信,似乎有些驚訝,但幾天沒跟我說什麼;霍姆斯船長回來之後,他拿給他看,問他認不認識基思,他是什麼樣的人;又補充說,他認為此人一定很缺乏判斷力,居然想到幫一個距離成年還差三年的男孩開業。霍姆斯盡他所能說了些贊成計劃的話,但我父親明確認為不適當,最後斷然拒絕。然後他寫了封客氣的信給威廉爵士,感謝他好意提供贊助,但婉拒暫時幫我開業,因為他認為我太年輕,不夠資格被託付管理一項這麼重要、準備又必須這麼昂貴的生意。

passages.original: My friend and companion Collins, who was a clerk in the post-office, pleas'd with the account I gave him of my new country, determined to go thither also; and, while I waited for my father's determination, he set out before me by land to Rhode Island, leaving his books, which were a pretty collection of mathematicks and natural philosophy, to come with mine and me to New York, where he propos'd to wait for me.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅朋友同伴柯林斯,係郵局嘅文員,對我講嘅新地方好滿意,決定都去嗰度;我等緊我爸爸嘅決定時,佢先行由陸路去羅得島,將佢啲書(一批相當好嘅數學同自然哲學藏書)留低,同我嘅書同我一齊去紐約,佢打算喺嗰度等我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的朋友同伴柯林斯,是郵局的文員,對我講的新地方很滿意,決定也去那裡;我等著我父親的決定時,他先行由陸路去羅得島,把他的書(一批相當好的數學和自然哲學藏書)留下,和我的書與我一起去紐約,他打算在那裡等我。

passages.original: My father, tho' he did not approve Sir William's proposition, was yet pleas'd that I had been able to obtain so advantageous a character from a person of such note where I had resided, and that I had been so industrious and careful as to equip myself so handsomely in so short a time; therefore, seeing no prospect of an accommodation between my brother and me, he gave his consent to my returning again to Philadelphia, advis'd me to behave respectfully to the people there, endeavor to obtain the general esteem, and avoid lampooning and libeling, to which he thought I had too much inclination; telling me, that by steady industry and a prudent parsimony I might save enough by the time I was one-and-twenty to set me up; and that, if I came near the matter, he would help me out with the rest. This was all I could obtain, except some small gifts as tokens of his and my mother's love, when I embark'd again for New York, now with their approbation and their blessing.
passages.vernacular: 我爸爸雖然不贊成威廉爵士嘅提議,但仍然高興我能夠喺我住過嘅地方,從一個咁有名望嘅人獲得咁有利嘅評價,亦高興我咁勤奮謹慎,短時間內就將自己裝備得咁體面;所以,見到我同哥哥冇和解嘅希望,佢同意我再返費城,勸我對嗰度嘅人要恭敬,努力贏得大家尊重,避免諷刺同誹謗(佢覺得我太傾向呢啲);話只要持續勤奮、審慎節儉,我廿一歲時可以儲夠錢開業;如果我接近目標,佢會幫我補足其餘。除咗少少禮物作為佢同我媽媽嘅愛心表示之外,我只得到呢啲;我再次乘船去紐約,今次得到佢哋同意同祝福。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我父親雖然不贊成威廉爵士的提議,但仍然高興我能夠在我住過的地方,從一個這麼有名望的人獲得這麼有利的評價,也高興我這麼勤奮謹慎,短時間內就把自己裝備得這麼體面;所以,見到我和哥哥沒有和解的希望,他同意我再回費城,勸我對那裡的人要恭敬,努力贏得大家尊重,避免諷刺和誹謗(他覺得我太傾向這些);說只要持續勤奮、審慎節儉,我二十一歲時可以儲夠錢開業;如果我接近目標,他會幫我補足其餘。除了一點禮物作為他和我母親的愛心表示之外,我只得到這些;我再次乘船去紐約,這次得到他們的同意和祝福。

passages.original: The sloop putting in at Newport, Rhode Island, I visited my brother John, who had been married and settled there some years. He received me very affectionately, for he always lov'd me. A friend of his, one Vernon, having some money due to him in Pensilvania, about thirty-five pounds currency, desired I would receive it for him, and keep it till I had his directions what to remit it in. Accordingly, he gave me an order. This afterwards occasion'd me a good deal of uneasiness.
passages.vernacular: 單桅帆船停靠羅得島嘅新港,我探望咗我哥哥約翰,佢已經結婚並喺嗰度定居咗幾年。佢好親切咁接待我,因為佢一向疼我。佢一個朋友,叫弗農,喺賓夕法尼亞有啲錢欠佢,大約三十五鎊當地貨幣,希望我替佢收,並保管直到佢指示點匯。於是佢畀咗張委託書我。呢件事後來令我好不安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 單桅帆船停靠羅得島的新港,我探望了我哥哥約翰,他已經結婚並在那裡定居了幾年。他很親切地接待我,因為他一向疼我。他一個朋友,叫弗農,在賓夕法尼亞有些錢欠他,大約三十五鎊當地貨幣,希望我替他收,並保管直到他指示怎樣匯。於是他給了張委託書給我。這件事後來使我非常不安。

passages.original: At Newport we took in a number of passengers for New York, among which were two young women, companions, and a grave, sensible, matron-like Quaker woman, with her attendants. I had shown an obliging readiness to do her some little services, which impress'd her I suppose with a degree of good will toward me; therefore, when she saw a daily growing familiarity between me and the two young women, which they appear'd to encourage, she took me aside, and said: "Young man, I am concern'd for thee, as thou has no friend with thee, and seems not to know much of the world, or of the snares youth is expos'd to; depend upon it, those are very bad women; I can see it in all their actions; and if thee art not upon thy guard, they will draw thee into some danger; they are strangers to thee, and I advise thee, in a friendly concern for thy welfare, to have no acquaintance with them." As I seem'd at first not to think so ill of them as she did, she mentioned some things she had observ'd and heard that had escap'd my notice, but now convinc'd me she was right. I thank'd her for her kind advice, and promis'd to follow it. When we arriv'd at New York, they told me where they liv'd, and invited me to come and see them; but I avoided it, and it was well I did; for the next day the captain miss'd a silver spoon and some other things, that had been taken out of his cabbin, and, knowing that these were a couple of strumpets, he got a warrant to search their lodgings, found the stolen goods, and had the thieves punish'd. So, tho' we had escap'd a sunken rock, which we scrap'd upon in the passage, I thought this escape of rather more importance to me.
passages.vernacular: 喺新港,我哋接載咗一批去紐約嘅乘客,當中有兩個年輕女子,係同伴,同一個嚴肅、明理、似主婦嘅貴格會婦人同佢嘅隨從。我曾經好熱心咁為佢做過啲小服務,我諗令佢對我有啲好感;所以當佢見到我同兩個年輕女子日漸熟絡,而佢哋似乎鼓勵,佢就拉我到一邊講:「後生仔,我替你擔心,因為你冇朋友同行,似乎對世情,或者青年人會遇到嘅陷阱了解唔多;你要相信,嗰啲係好壞嘅女人;我從佢哋所有行為睇得出;如果你唔提防,佢哋會將你拖入危險;佢哋對你係陌生人,我以友善嘅關心你嘅福祉,勸你唔好同佢哋有交往。」我起初似乎冇佢咁睇佢哋咁差,佢就提到佢觀察同聽到、我冇留意到嘅一啲事,而家令我相信佢啱。我多謝佢嘅好意勸告,答應跟從。我哋到紐約之後,佢哋話畀我知佢哋住邊,邀請我去探佢哋;我避開咗,幸好咁做;因為第二日船長發現唔見咗一隻銀匙同其他啲嘢,係從佢艙房攞走嘅,知道呢兩個係妓女,就拎手令搜查佢哋住處,搜到贓物,令賊人受到懲罰。所以,雖然我哋避過咗一塊沉落水底嘅礁石(我哋航行時擦過),我覺得呢次避過對我更重要。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在新港,我們接載了一批去紐約的乘客,其中有兩個年輕女子,是同伴,和一個嚴肅、明理、像主婦般的貴格會婦人與她的隨從。我曾經很熱心地為她做過些小服務,我想使她對我有些好感;所以當她看到我和兩個年輕女子日漸熟絡,而她們似乎鼓勵,她就拉我到一邊說:「年輕人,我替你擔心,因為你沒有朋友同行,似乎對世情,或者青年人會遇到的陷阱了解不多;你要相信,那些是很壞的女人;我從她們所有行為看得出;如果你不提防,她們會把你拖入危險;她們對你是陌生人,我以友善的關心你的福祉,勸你不要和她們有交往。」我起初似乎沒有她那樣把她們看得那麼壞,她就提到她觀察和聽到、我沒留意到的一些事,現在使我相信她是對的。我感謝她的好意勸告,答應聽從。我們到紐約之後,她們告訴我她們住哪裡,邀請我去探她們;我避開了,幸好這樣做;因為第二天船長發現不見了一隻銀匙和其他一些東西,是從他艙房拿走的,知道這兩個是妓女,就拿搜查令搜查她們住處,搜到贓物,使賊人受到懲罰。所以,雖然我們避過了一塊沉在水底的礁石(我們航行時擦過),我覺得這次避過對我更重要。

chapters.title: Collins, Keimer and Ralph 柯林斯、凱默與拉爾夫

passages.original: At New York I found my friend Collins, who had arriv'd there some time before me. We had been intimate from children, and had read the same books together; but he had the advantage of more time for reading and studying, and a wonderful genius for mathematical learning, in which he far outstript me. While I liv'd in Boston most of my hours of leisure for conversation were spent with him, and he continu'd a sober as well as an industrious lad; was much respected for his learning by several of the clergy and other gentlemen, and seemed to promise making a good figure in life. But, during my absence, he had acquir'd a habit of sotting with brandy; and I found by his own account, and what I heard from others, that he had been drunk every day since his arrival at New York, and behav'd very oddly. He had gam'd, too, and lost his money, so that I was oblig'd to discharge his lodgings, and defray his expenses to and at Philadelphia, which prov'd extremely inconvenient to me.
passages.vernacular: 喺紐約,我見到我朋友柯林斯,佢比我早到嗰度一段時間。我哋由細玩到大,一齊讀過同樣嘅書;不過佢有更多時間讀書同研究,而且對數學有驚人嘅天分,遠遠拋離我。我喺波士頓住嘅時候,大部分有空傾偈嘅時間都同佢一齊度過;佢一直係個清醒而且勤奮嘅後生,因為學問被好幾位牧師同其他紳士好尊重,似乎有希望喺人生中混出名堂。但係我離開期間,佢染上咗飲白蘭地飲到爛醉嘅習慣;我從佢自己嘅講法同聽返別人講,發現佢自到紐約之後每日都醉,行為好古怪。佢又賭錢輸咗錢,所以我要幫佢清付住宿費,同埋佢去費城同喺費城嘅開支,令我極之不便。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在紐約,我見到我朋友柯林斯,他比我早到那裡一段時間。我們從小玩到大,一起讀過同樣的書;不過他有更多時間讀書和研究,而且對數學有驚人的天分,遠遠超過我。我在波士頓住的時候,大部分有空聊天的時間都和他一起度過;他一直是個清醒而且勤奮的年輕人,因為學問被好幾位牧師和其他紳士很尊重,似乎有希望在人生中闖出名堂。但是我離開期間,他染上了喝白蘭地喝到爛醉的習慣;我從他自己的說法和聽別人說,發現他自到紐約之後每天都醉,行為很古怪。他又賭錢輸了錢,所以我要幫他付清住宿費,以及他去費城和在費城的開支,使我極其不便。

passages.original: The then governor of New York, Burnet (son of Bishop Burnet), hearing from the captain that a young man, one of his passengers, had a great many books, desir'd he would bring me to see him. I waited upon him accordingly, and should have taken Collins with me but that he was not sober. The gov'r. treated me with great civility, show'd me his library, which was a very large one, and we had a good deal of conversation about books and authors. This was the second governor who had done me the honor to take notice of me; which, to a poor boy like me, was very pleasing.
passages.vernacular: 當時紐約嘅省督伯內特(伯內特主教嘅兒子),從船長口中聽到有個後生乘客有好多書,希望船長帶我去見佢。我於是去拜訪佢,本來會帶柯林斯一齊去,不過佢唔清醒。省督好有禮貌咁招待我,帶我睇佢嘅圖書館,好大嘅一個,我哋就書同作者傾咗好多。呢位係第二位賞面留意我嘅省督;對一個似我咁貧窮嘅男孩嚟講,呢點好令人高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當時紐約的省督伯內特(伯內特主教的兒子),從船長口中聽到有個年輕乘客有很多書,希望船長帶我去見他。我於是去拜訪他,本來會帶柯林斯一起去,不過他不清醒。省督很有禮貌地招待我,帶我看他的圖書館,很大的一個,我們就書和作者聊了很多。這位是第二位賞臉留意我的省督;對一個像我這樣貧窮的男孩來說,這一點很令人高興。

passages.original: We proceeded to Philadelphia. I received on the way Vernon's money, without which we could hardly have finish'd our journey. Collins wished to be employ'd in some counting-house, but, whether they discover'd his dramming by his breath, or by his behaviour, tho' he had some recommendations, he met with no success in any application, and continu'd lodging and boarding at the same house with me, and at my expense. Knowing I had that money of Vernon's, he was continually borrowing of me, still promising repayment as soon as he should be in business. At length he had got so much of it that I was distress'd to think what I should do in case of being call'd on to remit it.
passages.vernacular: 我哋繼續去費城。途中我收到弗農嗰筆錢,冇咗佢,我哋幾乎冇辦法完成旅程。柯林斯想喺某間賬房搵份工,不過,有人話佢哋由佢口氣,或者由佢行為發現佢飲酒,雖然佢有幾封推薦信,每次申請都冇成功,繼續同我住同一間屋、食同一間,由我出錢。佢知道我有弗農嗰筆錢,就不斷向我借,不停咁承諾一有工做就還。最後佢攞咗咁多,我一諗到萬一被要求匯返出去應該點算就好苦惱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們繼續去費城。途中我收到弗農那筆錢,沒有它,我們幾乎沒辦法完成旅程。柯林斯想在某間賬房找份工作,不過,不知是他們從他的口氣,還是從他的行為發現他飲酒,雖然他有幾封推薦信,每次申請都沒成功,繼續跟我住同一間屋、吃同一間,由我出錢。他知道我有弗農那筆錢,就不斷向我借,不停地承諾一有工作就還。最後他拿了這麼多,我一想到萬一被要求匯回去該怎麼辦就很苦惱。

passages.original: His drinking continu'd, about which we sometimes quarrell'd; for, when a little intoxicated, he was very fractious. Once, in a boat on the Delaware with some other young men, he refused to row in his turn. "I will be row'd home," says he. "We will not row you," says I. "You must, or stay all night on the water," says he, "just as you please." The others said, "Let us row; what signifies it?" But, my mind being soured with his other conduct, I continu'd to refuse. So he swore he would make me row, or throw me overboard; and coming along, stepping on the thwarts, toward me, when he came up and struck at me, I clapped my hand under his crutch, and, rising, pitched him head-foremost into the river. I knew he was a good swimmer, and so was under little concern about him; but before he could get round to lay hold of the boat, we had with a few strokes pull'd her out of his reach; and ever when he drew near the boat, we ask'd if he would row, striking a few strokes to slide her away from him. He was ready to die with vexation, and obstinately would not promise to row. However, seeing him at last beginning to tire, we lifted him in and brought him home dripping wet in the evening. We hardly exchang'd a civil word afterwards, and a West India captain, who had a commission to procure a tutor for the sons of a gentleman at Barbadoes, happening to meet with him, agreed to carry him thither. He left me then, promising to remit me the first money he should receive in order to discharge the debt; but I never heard of him after.
passages.vernacular: 佢繼續飲酒,我哋有時為此爭吵;因為佢略有醉意嗰陣,好易發脾氣。有一次,喺德拉瓦河一艘船上,同其他幾個後生一齊,輪到佢划船佢唔肯。佢講:「我要人划我返去。」我講:「我哋唔會划你。」佢講:「你哋一定要,否則成晚留喺水上,隨便你。」其他人講:「我哋划啦,有咩所謂?」不過,我因為佢其他行為而心情惡劣,繼續拒絕。所以佢發誓要逼我划,或者將我拋落水;佢沿住船板踏過嚟,行到我面前向我出手打,我用手托住佢嘅胯下,站起身,將佢頭先腳後拋落河。我知道佢游水好,所以對佢冇太擔心;但係佢未游到船邊抓住船之前,我哋已經幾下划槳將船拉離佢手可及嘅範圍;每次佢接近船,我哋就問佢肯唔肯划,同時划幾下將船滑開。佢氣到想死,頑固咁唔肯答應划。不過,見到佢最後開始疲倦,我哋就將佢拉上船,傍晚帶住滴水嘅佢返屋企。之後我哋幾乎冇講過一句客氣話;一個西印度船長,受託替巴貝多一位紳士嘅兒子搵個家庭教師,碰巧遇到佢,同意帶佢去嗰度。佢於是離開我,答應一收到第一筆錢就匯畀我還債;但我之後再冇聽到過佢嘅消息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他繼續喝酒,我們有時為此爭吵;因為他略有醉意的時候,很容易發脾氣。有一次,在德拉瓦河一艘船上,和其他幾個年輕人一起,輪到他划船他不肯。他說:「我要人划我回去。」我說:「我們不會划你。」他說:「你們一定要,否則整晚留在水上,隨便你。」其他人說:「我們划吧,有什麼所謂?」不過,我因為他其他行為而心情惡劣,繼續拒絕。所以他發誓要逼我划,或者把我拋下水;他沿著船板踏過來,走到我面前向我出手打,我用手托住他的胯下,站起身,把他頭朝前拋進河裡。我知道他游泳很好,所以對他沒太擔心;但是他還沒游到船邊抓住船之前,我們已經幾下划槳把船拉離他手可及的範圍;每次他接近船,我們就問他肯不肯划,同時划幾下把船滑開。他氣得要死,頑固地不肯答應划。不過,見他最後開始疲倦,我們就把他拉上船,傍晚帶著滴水的他回家。之後我們幾乎沒說過一句客氣話;一個西印度船長,受託替巴貝多一位紳士的兒子找個家庭教師,碰巧遇到他,同意帶他去那裡。他於是離開我,答應一收到第一筆錢就匯給我還債;但我之後再沒聽到過他的消息。

passages.original: The breaking into this money of Vernon's was one of the first great errata of my life; and this affair show'd that my father was not much out in his judgment when he suppos'd me too young to manage business of importance. But Sir William, on reading his letter, said he was too prudent. There was great difference in persons; and discretion did not always accompany years, nor was youth always without it. "And since he will not set you up," says he, "I will do it myself. Give me an inventory of the things necessary to be had from England, and I will send for them. You shall repay me when you are able; I am resolv'd to have a good printer here, and I am sure you must succeed." This was spoken with such an appearance of cordiality, that I had not the least doubt of his meaning what he said. I had hitherto kept the proposition of my setting up, a secret in Philadelphia, and I still kept it. Had it been known that I depended on the governor, probably some friend, that knew him better, would have advis'd me not to rely on him, as I afterwards heard it as his known character to be liberal of promises which he never meant to keep. Yet, unsolicited as he was by me, how could I think his generous offers insincere? I believ'd him one of the best men in the world.
passages.vernacular: 動用弗農嗰筆錢,係我人生第一批大「勘誤」之一;而呢件事顯示,我爸爸認為我太年輕唔能管理重要生意,判斷並冇錯得太遠。不過威廉爵士讀咗我爸爸封信之後,話佢太謹慎。人與人差別好大;審慎唔一定隨年齡而至,青年人亦唔一定冇。佢講:「既然佢唔肯幫你開業,我自己嚟。你將需要從英國買嘅嘢開張清單畀我,我會訂購。你有能力嘅時候再還我;我決心喺度有個好印刷商,我肯定你一定會成功。」呢番話講得咁親切,我一啲都唔懷疑佢講嘅係真心。我一直對費城嘅人保密我開業嘅提議,仍然保密。如果人哋知道我倚靠省督,可能有個更了解佢嘅朋友,會勸我唔好倚靠佢,因為我後來聽講,佢出名慷慨許諾卻從無意兌現。不過,佢提出慷慨提議,我並冇懇求過,我點可能諗佢嘅提議唔真誠?我相信佢係世上最好嘅人之一。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動用弗農那筆錢,是我人生第一批大「勘誤」之一;而這件事顯示,我父親認為我太年輕不能管理重要生意,判斷並沒錯得太遠。不過威廉爵士讀了我父親那封信之後,說他太謹慎。人與人差別很大;審慎不一定隨年齡而來,青年人也不一定沒有。他說:「既然他不肯幫你開業,我自己來。你把需要從英國買的東西開張清單給我,我會訂購。你有能力的時候再還我;我決心在這裡有個好印刷商,我肯定你一定會成功。」這番話說得這麼親切,我一點都不懷疑他說的是真心。我一直對費城的人保密我開業的提議,仍然保密。如果別人知道我倚靠省督,可能有個更了解他的朋友,會勸我不要倚靠他,因為我後來聽說,他出名慷慨許諾卻從無意兌現。不過,他提出慷慨的提議,我並沒懇求過,我怎麼可能認為他的提議不真誠?我相信他是世上最好的人之一。

passages.original: I presented him an inventory of a little print'g-house, amounting by my computation to about one hundred pounds sterling. He lik'd it, but ask'd me if my being on the spot in England to chuse the types, and see that every thing was good of the kind, might not be of some advantage. "Then," says he, "when there, you may make acquaintances, and establish correspondences in the bookselling and stationery way." I agreed that this might be advantageous. "Then," says he, "get yourself ready to go with Annis;" which was the annual ship, and the only one at that time usually passing between London and Philadelphia. But it would be some months before Annis sail'd, so I continu'd working with Keimer, fretting about the money Collins had got from me, and in daily apprehensions of being call'd upon by Vernon, which, however, did not happen for some years after.
passages.vernacular: 我畀咗一份小印刷所嘅清單佢,按我計算大約一百英鎊。佢滿意,不過問我如果親身去英國揀鉛字、確保每樣東西都是同類中最好嘅,會唔會有好處。佢講:「去到嗰度,你仲可以結識人,建立書籍同文具買賣嘅聯繫。」我同意呢點可能有利。佢講:「咁你準備好同『安尼斯號』一齊去。」嗰艘係每年一班嘅船,亦係當時通常往來倫敦同費城唯一嘅船。不過「安尼斯號」要過幾個月先開,所以我繼續同凱默做嘢,為柯林斯攞咗我嘅錢而煩惱,日日擔心弗農會叫我還,不過呢件事幾年後先發生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我給了他一份小印刷所的清單,按我計算大約一百英鎊。他滿意,不過問我如果親身去英國挑鉛字、確保每樣東西都是同類中最好的,會不會有好處。他說:「到了那裡,你還可以結識人,建立書籍和文具買賣的聯繫。」我同意這一點可能有利。他說:「那你準備好跟『安尼斯號』一起去。」那艘是每年一班的船,也是當時通常往來倫敦和費城唯一的船。不過「安尼斯號」要過幾個月才開,所以我繼續跟凱默做事,為柯林斯拿了我的錢而煩惱,天天擔心弗農會叫我還,不過這件事幾年後才發生。

passages.original: I believe I have omitted mentioning that, in my first voyage from Boston, being becalm'd off Block Island, our people set about catching cod, and hauled up a great many. Hitherto I had stuck to my resolution of not eating animal food, and on this occasion consider'd, with my master Tryon, the taking every fish as a kind of unprovoked murder, since none of them had, or ever could do us any injury that might justify the slaughter. All this seemed very reasonable. But I had formerly been a great lover of fish, and, when this came hot out of the frying-pan, it smelt admirably well. I balanc'd some time between principle and inclination, till I recollected that, when the fish were opened, I saw smaller fish taken out of their stomachs; then thought I, "If you eat one another, I don't see why we mayn't eat you." So I din'd upon cod very heartily, and continued to eat with other people, returning only now and then occasionally to a vegetable diet. So convenient a thing it is to be a reasonable creature, since it enables one to find or make a reason for everything one has a mind to do.
passages.vernacular: 我相信我漏咗講:我第一次由波士頓出航時,喺布洛克島外海冇風,我哋船員就開始釣鱈魚,拉上嚟好多。直至當時,我仍堅持不食動物性食物嘅決心;今次我同我嘅導師特賴恩一樣,認為捕每條魚都係一種無端嘅謀殺,因為牠哋冇一條傷害過我哋,亦永遠不可能傷害我哋到足以為屠殺辯護。呢一切似乎都好合理。但係我以前好鍾意食魚,而當條魚熱辣辣由煎鍋攞出嚟,聞落去香到不得了。我喺原則同喜好之間掙扎咗一陣,直到我記起,魚被剖開嘅時候,我見到牠哋胃裡面有更細嘅魚;於是我諗:「你哋互相食,我睇唔出點解我哋唔可以食你哋。」於是我津津有味咁食咗鱈魚,之後同其他人一齊食,只係偶爾先返去食素。做一個有理性嘅生物真係方便,因為佢令人可以為自己想做嘅每件事,搵到或者作出一個理由。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我相信我漏講了:我第一次從波士頓出航時,在布洛克島外海沒有風,我們的船員就開始釣鱈魚,拉上來很多。直至當時,我仍堅持不吃動物性食物的決心;這次我和我的導師特賴恩一樣,認為捕每條魚都是一種無端的謀殺,因為牠們沒有一條傷害過我們,也永遠不可能傷害我們到足以為屠殺辯護。這一切似乎都很合理。但是我以前很喜歡吃魚,而當這條魚熱騰騰從煎鍋拿出來,聞起來香得不得了。我在原則和喜好之間掙扎了一陣,直到我記起,魚被剖開的時候,我看到牠們胃裡有更小的魚;於是我想:「你們互相吃,我看不出為什麼我們不可以吃你們。」於是我津津有味地吃了鱈魚,之後和其他人一起吃,只是偶爾才回去吃素。做一個有理性的生物真是方便,因為它使人可以為自己想做的每件事,找到或編造一個理由。

passages.original: Keimer and I liv'd on a pretty good familiar footing, and agreed tolerably well, for he suspected nothing of my setting up. He retained a great deal of his old enthusiasms and lov'd argumentation. We therefore had many disputations. I used to work him so with my Socratic method, and had trepann'd him so often by questions apparently so distant from any point we had in hand, and yet by degrees lead to the point, and brought him into difficulties and contradictions, that at last he grew ridiculously cautious, and would hardly answer me the most common question, without asking first, "What do you intend to infer from that?" However, it gave him so high an opinion of my abilities in the confuting way, that he seriously proposed my being his colleague in a project he had of setting up a new sect. He was to preach the doctrines, and I was to confound all opponents. When he came to explain with me upon the doctrines, I found several conundrums which I objected to, unless I might have my way a little too, and introduce some of mine.
passages.vernacular: 凱默同我相處得相當熟絡,相處尚算融洽,因為佢對我開業一事毫無懷疑。佢保留咗好多舊日嘅狂熱,鍾意辯論。所以我哋有好多爭論。我經常用我嘅蘇格拉底式方法對付佢,用一啲表面上同手上議題好遠嘅問題引佢上當,但又逐步引到重點,令佢陷入困難同矛盾,以致最後佢變得好笑咁謹慎,連最普通嘅問題都幾乎唔肯答我,除非先問:「你想由呢個推論出乜嘢?」不過,呢點令佢對我駁倒人嘅能力評價好高,以致佢認真咁提議我做佢嘅同伴,參與佢打算創立新教派嘅計劃。佢負責宣講教義,我負責駁倒所有反對者。佢同我解釋教義的時候,我發現幾個難解之處我反對,除非我亦可以有少少自己嘅主張,加入我嘅一啲嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 凱默和我相處得相當熟絡,相處尚算融洽,因為他對我開業一事毫無懷疑。他保留了許多舊日的狂熱,喜歡辯論。所以我們有許多爭論。我經常用我的蘇格拉底式方法對付他,用一些表面上同手上議題很遠的問題引他上當,但又逐步引到重點,使他陷入困難和矛盾,以致最後他變得可笑地謹慎,連最普通的問題都幾乎不肯回答我,除非先問:「你想由這個推論出什麼?」不過,這一點使他對我駁倒人的能力評價很高,以致他認真地提議我做他的同伴,參與他打算創立新教派的計劃。他負責宣講教義,我負責駁倒所有反對者。他和我解釋教義的時候,我發現幾個難解之處我反對,除非我也可以有一點自己的主張,加入我的一些東西。

passages.original: Keimer wore his beard at full length, because somewhere in the Mosaic law it is said, "Thou shalt not mar the corners of thy beard." He likewise kept the Seventh day, Sabbath; and these two points were essentials with him. I dislik'd both; but agreed to admit them upon condition of his adopting the doctrine of using no animal food. "I doubt," said he, "my constitution will not bear that." I assur'd him it would, and that he would be the better for it. He was usually a great glutton, and I promised myself some diversion in half starving him. He agreed to try the practice, if I would keep him company. I did so, and we held it for three months. We had our victuals dress'd, and brought to us regularly by a woman in the neighborhood, who had from me a list of forty dishes to be prepar'd for us at different times, in all which there was neither fish, flesh, nor fowl, and the whim suited me the better at this time from the cheapness of it, not costing us above eighteenpence sterling each per week. I have since kept several Lents most strictly, leaving the common diet for that, and that for the common, abruptly, without the least inconvenience, so that I think there is little in the advice of making those changes by easy gradations. I went on pleasantly, but poor Keimer suffered grievously, tired of the project, long'd for the flesh-pots of Egypt, and order'd a roast pig. He invited me and two women friends to dine with him; but, it being brought too soon upon table, he could not resist the temptation, and ate the whole before we came.
passages.vernacular: 凱默留長鬍鬚,因為摩西律法某處寫:「不可損壞你鬍鬚的周圍。」佢亦守第七日安息日;呢兩點對佢嚟講都係根本。我兩樣都唔鍾意,不過同意接受,條件係佢採用不食動物性食物嘅教義。佢講:「我怕我嘅體質受唔住。」我向佢保證受得住,而且對佢有益。佢通常好貪食,我預計半餓住佢會好有趣。佢同意試做,只要我陪佢。我照做,我哋堅持咗三個月。我哋嘅食物由附近一個女人煮好,定時送嚟;佢從我度攞到一份四十道菜嘅清單,不同時間準備畀我哋,全部冇魚、冇肉、冇禽;呢個怪念頭呢個時候更適合我,因為夠便宜,每人每星期唔使十八便士。我後來嚴格咁守過好幾次四旬齋,突然由平常飲食轉去齋食,又突然轉返,毫無不便,所以我覺得,逐漸轉換嘅建議其實冇太大道理。我愉快咁繼續,不過可憐嘅凱默受盡折磨,厭倦咗呢個計劃,渴望埃及嘅肉鍋,叫咗一隻烤乳豬。佢邀請我同兩位女性朋友同佢食飯;不過,乳豬太早上枱,佢抵受唔住誘惑,我哋未到,佢已經全部食晒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 凱默留長鬍鬚,因為摩西律法某處寫:「不可損壞你鬍鬚的周圍。」他也守第七日安息日;這兩點對他來說都是根本。我兩樣都不喜歡,不過同意接受,條件是他採用不吃動物性食物的教義。他說:「我怕我的體質受不了。」我向他保證受得住,而且對他有益。他通常很貪吃,我預計讓他半餓著會很有趣。他同意試做,只要我陪他。我照做,我們堅持了三個月。我們的食物由附近一個女人煮好,定時送來;她從我這裡拿到一份四十道菜的清單,不同時間準備給我們,全部沒有魚、沒有肉、沒有禽;這個怪念頭這時更適合我,因為夠便宜,每人每星期不到十八便士。我後來嚴格地守過好幾次四旬齋,突然從平常飲食轉去齋食,又突然轉回,毫無不便,所以我覺得,逐漸轉換的建議其實沒太大道理。我愉快地繼續,不過可憐的凱默受盡折磨,厭倦了這個計劃,渴望埃及的肉鍋,叫了一隻烤乳豬。他邀請我和兩位女性朋友和他吃飯;不過,乳豬太早上桌,他抵受不住誘惑,我們還沒到,他已經全部吃光。

passages.original: I had made some courtship during this time to Miss Read. I had a great respect and affection for her, and had some reason to believe she had the same for me; but, as I was about to take a long voyage, and we were both very young, only a little above eighteen, it was thought most prudent by her mother to prevent our going too far at present, as a marriage, if it was to take place, would be more convenient after my return, when I should be, as I expected, set up in my business. Perhaps, too, she thought my expectations not so well founded as I imagined them to be.
passages.vernacular: 呢段時間,我向里德小姐求過愛。我對佢好尊重同愛慕,亦有理由相信佢對我都一樣;不過,因為我快要遠航,我哋又都好年輕,只係十八歲多少少,佢媽媽覺得最審慎係防止我哋現階段發展太快,因為如果結婚,等我返嚟之後方便啲,到時我預計已經開業。或者,佢亦覺得我嘅期望唔似我想像咁有根據。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這段時間,我向里德小姐求過愛。我對她很尊重和愛慕,也有理由相信她對我也一樣;不過,因為我快要遠航,我們又都很年輕,只是十八歲多一點,她母親覺得最審慎是防止我們現階段發展太快,因為如果結婚,等我回來之後方便一些,到時我預計已經開業。也許,她也覺得我的期望不像我想像的那麼有根據。

passages.original: My chief acquaintances at this time were Charles Osborne, Joseph Watson, and James Ralph, all lovers of reading. The two first were clerks to an eminent scrivener or conveyancer in the town, Charles Brogden; the other was clerk to a merchant. Watson was a pious, sensible young man, of great integrity; the others rather more lax in their principles of religion, particularly Ralph, who, as well as Collins, had been unsettled by me, for which they both made me suffer. Osborne was sensible, candid, frank; sincere and affectionate to his friends; but, in literary matters, too fond of criticising. Ralph was ingenious, genteel in his manners, and extremely eloquent; I think I never knew a prettier talker. Both of them great admirers of poetry, and began to try their hands in little pieces. Many pleasant walks we four had together on Sundays into the woods, near Schuylkill, where we read to one another, and conferr'd on what we read.
passages.vernacular: 我當時主要嘅相識係查爾斯·奧斯本、約瑟夫·沃森同詹姆斯·拉爾夫,都係愛讀書嘅人。前兩個係鎮上一位著名代書人或者地契轉讓人查爾斯·布羅格登嘅文員;另一個係一個商人嘅文員。沃森係個虔誠、明理、品行端正嘅後生;其他人宗教原則較為鬆散,尤其拉爾夫,同柯林斯一樣,被我動搖過,佢哋兩個都為此令我受苦。奧斯本明理、坦白、率直;對朋友真誠親切;不過喺文學事情上太鍾意批評。拉爾夫聰明、舉止文雅、極有口才;我諗我從來冇認識過更動聽嘅健談者。佢哋兩個都好欣賞詩,開始試寫小作品。我哋四個星期日經常愉快咁行入史古基爾河附近嘅樹林,互相朗讀,討論所讀嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我當時主要的相識是查爾斯·奧斯本、約瑟夫·沃森和詹姆斯·拉爾夫,都是愛讀書的人。前兩個是鎮上一位著名代書人或地契轉讓人查爾斯·布羅格登的文員;另一個是一個商人的文員。沃森是個虔誠、明理、品行端正的年輕人;其他人宗教原則較為鬆散,尤其拉爾夫,和柯林斯一樣,被我動搖過,他們兩個都為此讓我受苦。奧斯本明理、坦白、率直;對朋友真誠親切;不過在文學事情上太喜歡批評。拉爾夫聰明、舉止文雅、極有口才;我想我從來沒認識過更動聽的健談者。他們兩個都很欣賞詩,開始試寫小作品。我們四個星期日經常愉快地走進斯庫爾基爾河附近的樹林,互相朗讀,討論所讀的東西。

passages.original: Ralph was inclin'd to pursue the study of poetry, not doubting but he might become eminent in it, and make his fortune by it, alleging that the best poets must, when they first began to write, make as many faults as he did. Osborne dissuaded him, assur'd him he had no genius for poetry, and advis'd him to think of nothing beyond the business he was bred to; that, in the mercantile way, tho' he had no stock, he might, by his diligence and punctuality, recommend himself to employment as a factor, and in time acquire wherewith to trade on his own account. I approv'd the amusing one's self with poetry now and then, so far as to improve one's language, but no farther.
passages.vernacular: 拉爾夫傾向繼續學詩,毫不懷疑自己可以喺詩壇出名,靠詩發達,聲稱最好嘅詩人剛開始寫嘅時候,犯嘅錯同佢一樣多。奧斯本勸阻佢,向佢保證佢冇詩歌天分,勸佢唔好諗佢學慣行業以外嘅嘢;喺商業方面,雖然佢冇本錢,但靠勤奮同守時,可以推薦自己做代理商,時間久咗就可以賺夠錢自己做生意。我贊成偶爾玩玩詩作消遣,只要用嚟改進語言,但唔好再進。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拉爾夫傾向繼續學詩,毫不懷疑自己可以在詩壇出名,靠詩發達,聲稱最好的詩人剛開始寫的時候,犯的錯和他一樣多。奧斯本勸阻他,向他保證他沒有詩歌天分,勸他不要想他學慣行業以外的東西;在商業方面,雖然他沒有本錢,但靠勤奮和守時,可以推薦自己做代理商,時間久了就可以賺夠錢自己做生意。我贊成偶爾玩玩詩作消遣,只要用來改進語言,但不要再進一步。

passages.original: On this it was propos'd that we should each of us, at our next meeting, produce a piece of our own composing, in order to improve by our mutual observations, criticisms, and corrections. As language and expression were what we had in view, we excluded all considerations of invention by agreeing that the task should be a version of the eighteenth Psalm, which describes the descent of a Deity. When the time of our meeting drew nigh, Ralph called on me first, and let me know his piece was ready. I told him I had been busy, and, having little inclination, had done nothing. He then show'd me his piece for my opinion, and I much approv'd it, as it appear'd to me to have great merit. "Now," says he, "Osborne never will allow the least merit in any thing of mine, but makes 1000 criticisms out of mere envy. He is not so jealous of you; I wish, therefore, you would take this piece, and produce it as yours; I will pretend not to have had time, and so produce nothing. We shall then see what he will say to it." It was agreed, and I immediately transcrib'd it, that it might appear in my own hand.
passages.vernacular: 於是有人提議,我哋每人下次聚會要拿出一首自己作嘅作品,藉互相觀察、批評同修改嚟進步。因為我哋著眼於語言同表達,所以我哋同意題目係翻譯第十八篇詩篇(描寫神降臨),排除創作考慮。聚會時間臨近,拉爾夫先嚟搵我,話佢嘅作品準備好。我話我忙,又冇咩興趣,所以乜都冇做。佢於是拎佢嘅作品畀我睇,問我意見,我好贊成,覺得佢好有價值。佢講:「奧斯本從來唔肯承認我嘅任何嘢有半點價值,淨係出於妒忌就提一千個批評。佢冇咁妒忌你;所以我希望你拎呢首,當係你嘅作品拎出嚟;我扮冇時間,咁就乜都冇拎出嚟。咁我哋就睇佢點講。」大家同意,我即刻抄寫,令佢以我自己嘅筆跡出現。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是有人提議,我們每人下次聚會要拿出一首自己作的作品,藉互相觀察、批評和修改來進步。因為我們著眼於語言和表達,所以我們同意題目是翻譯第十八篇詩篇(描寫神降臨),排除創作的考慮。聚會時間臨近,拉爾夫先來找我,說他的作品準備好了。我說我忙,又沒什麼興趣,所以什麼都沒做。他於是拿他的作品給我看,問我意見,我很贊成,覺得很有價值。他說:「奧斯本從來不肯承認我的任何東西有半點價值,只出於妒忌就提一千個批評。他沒那麼妒忌你;所以我希望你拿這首,當作你的作品拿出來;我假裝沒時間,這樣就什麼都不拿出來。那我們就看他怎麼說。」大家同意,我立刻抄寫,讓它以我自己的筆跡出現。

passages.original: We met; Watson's performance was read; there were some beauties in it, but many defects. Osborne's was read; it was much better; Ralph did it justice; remarked some faults, but applauded the beauties. He himself had nothing to produce. I was backward; seemed desirous of being excused; had not had sufficient time to correct, etc.; but no excuse could be admitted; produce I must. It was read and repeated; Watson and Osborne gave up the contest, and join'd in applauding it. Ralph only made some criticisms, and propos'd some amendments; but I defended my text. Osborne was against Ralph, and told him he was no better a critic than poet, so he dropt the argument. As they two went home together, Osborne expressed himself still more strongly in favor of what he thought my production; having restrain'd himself before, as he said, lest I should think it flattery. "But who would have imagin'd," said he, "that Franklin had been capable of such a performance; such painting, such force, such fire! He has even improv'd the original. In his common conversation he seems to have no choice of words; he hesitates and blunders; and yet, good God! how he writes!" When we next met, Ralph discovered the trick we had plaid him, and Osborne was a little laught at.
passages.vernacular: 我哋聚會;沃森嘅作品被朗讀;有啲優點,不過缺點好多。奧斯本嘅被朗讀;好好多;拉爾夫公平對待,指出幾個缺點,但讚賞優點。佢自己冇嘢拎出嚟。我推搪,似乎希望獲得豁免,話冇足夠時間修改等等;不過冇借口被接受,我一定要拎出嚟。佢被朗讀同重複;沃森同奧斯本放棄競爭,一齊讚賞。拉爾夫只提出一啲批評同修改建議;不過我維護我嘅文本。奧斯本反對拉爾夫,話佢作為評論家唔比詩人好,所以佢放棄爭論。佢哋兩個一齊返屋企時,奧斯本更加強烈咁表示支持佢以為係我嘅作品;佢話之前一直克制,怕我以為係奉承。佢講:「但係邊個諗到富蘭克林居然有能力做出咁嘅作品;咁嘅描繪、咁嘅力量、咁嘅火焰!佢甚至改進咗原文。平時談話,佢似乎冇揀字嘅能力;佢猶豫同出錯;但係,天哪!佢寫嘢真係咁好!」我哋下次聚會時,拉爾夫揭穿咗我哋對佢玩嘅把戲,奧斯本被笑咗一下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們聚會;沃森的作品被朗讀;有些優點,不過缺點很多。奧斯本的被朗讀;好得多;拉爾夫公平對待,指出幾個缺點,但讚賞優點。他自己沒有東西拿出來。我推搪,似乎希望獲得豁免,說沒有足夠時間修改等等;不過沒有借口被接受,我一定要拿出來。它被朗讀和重複;沃森和奧斯本放棄競爭,一起讚賞。拉爾夫只提出一些批評和修改建議;不過我維護我的文本。奧斯本反對拉爾夫,說他作為評論家不比詩人好,所以他放棄爭論。他們兩個一起回家時,奧斯本更加強烈地表示支持他以為是我的作品;他說之前一直克制,怕我以為是奉承。他說:「但是誰想到富蘭克林居然有能力做出這樣的作品;這樣的描繪、這樣的力量、這樣的火焰!他甚至改進了原文。平時談話,他似乎沒有選字的能力;他猶豫又出錯;但是,天哪!他寫東西竟然這麼好!」我們下次聚會時,拉爾夫揭穿了我們對他玩的把戲,奧斯本被笑了一下。

passages.original: This transaction fixed Ralph in his resolution of becoming a poet. I did all I could to dissuade him from it, but he continued scribbling verses till Pope cured him. He became, however, a pretty good prose writer. More of him hereafter. But, as I may not have occasion again to mention the other two, I shall just remark here, that Watson died in my arms a few years after, much lamented, being the best of our set. Osborne went to the West Indies, where he became an eminent lawyer and made money, but died young. He and I had made a serious agreement, that the one who happen'd first to die should, if possible, make a friendly visit to the other, and acquaint him how he found things in that separate state. But he never fulfill'd his promise.
passages.vernacular: 呢件事令拉爾夫更堅定成為詩人嘅決心。我盡我所能勸阻佢,不過佢繼續亂寫詩,直到蒲柏醫好佢。不過,佢成為咗一個相當好嘅散文作家。之後再講佢。但我可能不會再有機會提另外兩個,所以我喺度簡單講一下:沃森幾年後死喺我懷中,好多人哀悼,佢係我哋一夥中最好嘅人。奧斯本去咗西印度群島,成為一位著名律師並賺到錢,但年紀輕輕就死咗。佢同我曾經認真協議,誰先死,可能的話就應該友好咁探訪另一個,話畀對方知道喺嗰個分離狀態入面情況如何。但佢從來冇履行承諾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這件事使拉爾夫更堅定成為詩人的決心。我盡我所能勸阻他,不過他繼續亂寫詩,直到蒲柏醫好他。不過,他成為了一個相當好的散文作家。之後再講他。但我可能不會再有機會提另外兩個,所以我在這裡簡單說一下:沃森幾年後死在我懷中,很多人哀悼,他是我們這夥人中最好的。奧斯本去了西印度群島,成為一位著名律師並賺到錢,但年紀輕輕就死了。他和我曾經認真協議,誰先死,可能的話就應該友好地探訪另一個,告訴對方在那個分離狀態裡情況如何。但他從來沒履行承諾。

chapters.title: Cheated in London 倫敦受騙與立足

passages.original: The governor, seeming to like my company, had me frequently to his house, and his setting me up was always mention'd as a fixed thing. I was to take with me letters recommendatory to a number of his friends, besides the letter of credit to furnish me with the necessary money for purchasing the press and types, paper, etc. For these letters I was appointed to call at different times, when they were to be ready, but a future time was still named. Thus he went on till the ship, whose departure too had been several times postponed, was on the point of sailing. Then, when I call'd to take my leave and receive the letters, his secretary, Dr. Bard, came out to me and said the governor was extremely busy in writing, but would be down at Newcastle before the ship, and there the letters would be delivered to me.
passages.vernacular: 省督似乎鍾意我嘅陪伴,經常叫我去佢屋,而佢幫我開業呢件事,一直都當作已經定咗嘅事提起。除咗信用狀,畀我購買印刷機、鉛字、紙張等需要嘅錢之外,我仲會帶住推薦信去見佢好多朋友。為咗呢啲信,我被安排喺不同時間去攞,話到時會準備好,不過總係訂一個將來嘅時間。佢就咁拖,直到船(佢嘅開航日期亦延遲咗好幾次)快要開。然後,我去告辭同攞信嘅時候,佢嘅秘書巴德醫生出嚟同我講,省督寫字寫得極忙,不過會喺船之前去到紐卡斯爾,到時信會交畀我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 省督似乎喜歡我的陪伴,經常叫我去他家,而他幫我開業這件事,一直都當作已經定了的事提起。除了信用狀,供我購買印刷機、鉛字、紙張等需要的錢之外,我還會帶著推薦信去見他許多朋友。為了這些信,我被安排在不同時間去拿,說到時會準備好,不過總是訂一個將來的時間。他就這樣拖,直到船(它的開航日期也延遲了好幾次)快要開。然後,我去告辭和拿信的時候,他的秘書巴德醫生出來對我說,省督寫字寫得極忙,不過會在船之前到紐卡斯爾,到時信會交給我。

passages.original: Ralph, though married, and having one child, had determined to accompany me in this voyage. It was thought he intended to establish a correspondence, and obtain goods to sell on commission; but I found afterwards, that, thro' some discontent with his wife's relations, he purposed to leave her on their hands, and never return again. Having taken leave of my friends, and interchang'd some promises with Miss Read, I left Philadelphia in the ship, which anchor'd at Newcastle. The governor was there; but when I went to his lodging, the secretary came to me from him with the civillest message in the world, that he could not then see me, being engaged in business of the utmost importance, but should send the letters to me on board, wish'd me heartily a good voyage and a speedy return, etc. I returned on board a little puzzled, but still not doubting.
passages.vernacular: 拉爾夫雖然已婚,又有一個孩子,決心陪我呢次航行。有人以為佢打算建立聯繫,取得貨物以佣金方式售賣;但我後來發現,因為同太太嘅親戚有啲不滿,佢打算將太太丟畀佢哋,永遠唔返嚟。同朋友告別,又同里德小姐互相許下一啲承諾之後,我乘船離開費城,船停泊喺紐卡斯爾。省督喺嗰度;不過我去佢住處嗰陣,秘書帶佢嘅口訊嚟見我,用世上最客氣嘅話,話佢而家見唔到我,因為有極重要嘅事務,不過會將信送上船,衷心祝我一路順風、早日返嚟等等。我返上船,有啲疑惑,但仍然冇懷疑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拉爾夫雖然已婚,又有一個孩子,決心陪我這次航行。有人以為他打算建立聯繫,取得貨物以佣金方式出售;但我後來發現,因為對妻子的親戚有些不滿,他打算把妻子丟給他們,永遠不回來。和朋友告別,又和里德小姐互相許下一些承諾之後,我乘船離開費城,船停泊在紐卡斯爾。省督在那裡;不過我去他住處時,秘書帶他的口訊來見我,用世上最客氣的話,說他現在見不到我,因為有極重要的事務,不過會把信送上船,衷心祝我一路順風、早日回來等等。我回到船上,有些疑惑,但仍然沒有懷疑。

passages.original: Mr. Andrew Hamilton, a famous lawyer of Philadelphia, had taken passage in the same ship for himself and son, and with Mr. Denham, a Quaker merchant, and Messrs. Onion and Russel, masters of an iron work in Maryland, had engag'd the great cabin; so that Ralph and I were forced to take up with a berth in the steerage, and none on board knowing us, were considered as ordinary persons. But Mr. Hamilton and his son (it was James, since governor) return'd from Newcastle to Philadelphia, the father being recall'd by a great fee to plead for a seized ship; and, just before we sail'd, Colonel French coming on board, and showing me great respect, I was more taken notice of, and, with my friend Ralph, invited by the other gentlemen to come into the cabin, there being now room. Accordingly, we remov'd thither.
passages.vernacular: 費城著名律師安德魯·漢密爾頓先生,同佢兒子一齊搭咗同一艘船,同貴格會商人德納姆先生,以及馬里蘭一間鐵廠嘅老闆奧尼恩同拉塞爾兩位先生,包咗大艙;所以拉爾夫同我只好住底艙嘅一個鋪位,船上冇人認識我哋,被當成普通人。不過漢密爾頓先生同佢兒子(係詹姆斯,後來做咗省督)由紐卡斯爾返費城,因為爸爸被一筆高昂律師費召返去為一艘被扣押嘅船辯護;而就喺我哋開船前,弗倫奇上校上船,對我好尊重,我多咗人留意,同我朋友拉爾夫一齊被其他紳士邀請入艙,因為而家有位置。於是我哋搬過去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 費城著名律師安德魯·漢密爾頓先生,與他兒子一起搭了同一艘船,與貴格會商人德納姆先生,以及馬里蘭一間鐵廠的老闆奧尼恩和拉塞爾兩位先生,包了大艙;所以拉爾夫和我只好住底艙的一個鋪位,船上沒有人認識我們,被當成普通人。不過漢密爾頓先生和他兒子(是詹姆斯,後來做了省督)從紐卡斯爾回費城,因為父親被一筆高昂律師費召回去為一艘被扣押的船辯護;而就在我們開船前,弗倫奇上校上船,對我很尊重,我多了人留意,與我朋友拉爾夫一起被其他紳士邀請進艙,因為現在有位置。於是我們搬過去。

passages.original: Understanding that Colonel French had brought on board the governor's despatches, I ask'd the captain for those letters that were to be under my care. He said all were put into the bag together and he could not then come at them; but, before we landed in England, I should have an opportunity of picking them out; so I was satisfied for the present, and we proceeded on our voyage. We had a sociable company in the cabin, and lived uncommonly well, having the addition of all Mr. Hamilton's stores, who had laid in plentifully. In this passage Mr. Denham contracted a friendship for me that continued during his life. The voyage was otherwise not a pleasant one, as we had a great deal of bad weather.
passages.vernacular: 知道弗倫奇上校已經將省督嘅公文帶上船,我問船長要交我保管嗰啲信。佢話所有信已經放咗落同一個袋,而家攞唔到;不過喺我哋抵達英國之前,我會有機會揀出嚟;我暫時滿意,我哋繼續航程。我哋艙內有一班合群嘅同伴,生活特別好,因為多咗漢密爾頓先生所有嘅補給,佢準備得好充足。呢次航行中,德納姆先生同我建立咗友誼,維持到佢去世。除此之外,航行並不愉快,因為天氣惡劣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 知道弗倫奇上校已經把省督的公文帶上船,我問船長要交給我保管的那些信。他說所有信已經放進同一個袋子,現在拿不到;不過在我們抵達英國之前,我會有機會挑出來;我暫時滿意,我們繼續航程。我們艙內有一班合群的同伴,生活特別好,因為多了漢密爾頓先生所有的補給,他準備得很充足。這次航行中,德納姆先生與我建立了友誼,維持到他去世。除此之外,航行並不愉快,因為天氣惡劣。

passages.original: When we came into the Channel, the captain kept his word with me, and gave me an opportunity of examining the bag for the governor's letters. I found none upon which my name was put as under my care. I picked out six or seven, that, by the handwriting, I thought might be the promised letters, especially as one of them was directed to Basket, the king's printer, and another to some stationer. We arriv'd in London the 24th of December, 1724. I waited upon the stationer, who came first in my way, delivering the letter as from Governor Keith. "I don't know such a person," says he; but, opening the letter, "O! this is from Riddlesden. I have lately found him to be a compleat rascal, and I will have nothing to do with him, nor receive any letters from him." So, putting the letter into my hand, he turn'd on his heel and left me to serve some customer. I was surprized to find these were not the governor's letters; and, after recollecting and comparing circumstances, I began to doubt his sincerity. I found my friend Denham, and opened the whole affair to him. He let me into Keith's character; told me there was not the least probability that he had written any letters for me; that no one, who knew him, had the smallest dependence on him; and he laught at the notion of the governor's giving me a letter of credit, having, as he said, no credit to give. On my expressing some concern about what I should do, he advised me to endeavor getting some employment in the way of my business. "Among the printers here," said he, "you will improve yourself, and when you return to America, you will set up to greater advantage."
passages.vernacular: 我哋入咗英倫海峽之後,船長信守承諾,畀我機會檢查個袋找省督嘅信。我發現冇一封寫住交我保管。我揀咗六七封,憑筆跡我以為可能係承諾過嘅信,尤其其中一封寫畀國王嘅印刷商巴斯克特,另一封寫畀某個文具商。我哋1724年12月24日抵達倫敦。我拜訪最先順路嘅文具商,將信當成基思省督寫嘅交畀佢。佢講:「我唔認識呢個人。」不過拆開信:「噢!呢封係里德斯登寫嘅。我最近發現佢係個十足嘅無賴,我同佢冇任何關係,亦唔收佢嘅任何信。」於是佢將信塞返我手,轉身走開去招呼客人。我驚訝地發現呢啲唔係省督嘅信;回想同比較各種情況之後,我開始懷疑佢嘅誠意。我搵到朋友德納姆,將整件事向佢和盤托出。佢讓我了解基思嘅為人;話佢完全冇可能為我寫過任何信;認識佢嘅人冇一個對佢有半點倚賴;對於省督畀我信用狀嘅想法,佢笑咗,話佢冇信用可畀。我表示擔心應該點算,佢勸我設法搵一份自己行業嘅工作。佢講:「喺呢度嘅印刷商當中,你會進步,等你返美洲,就可以更有利咁開業。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們進了英倫海峽之後,船長信守承諾,給我機會檢查那個袋子找省督的信。我發現沒有一封寫著交我保管。我挑了六七封,憑筆跡我以為可能是承諾過的信,尤其其中一封寫給國王的印刷商巴斯克特,另一封寫給某個文具商。我們1724年12月24日抵達倫敦。我拜訪最先順路的文具商,把信當成基思省督寫的交給他。他說:「我不認識這個人。」不過拆開信:「噢!這封是里德斯登寫的。我最近發現他是個十足的無賴,我與他沒有任何關係,也不收他的任何信。」於是他把信塞回我手裡,轉身走開去招呼客人。我驚訝地發現這些不是省督的信;回想並比較各種情況之後,我開始懷疑他的誠意。我找到朋友德納姆,把整件事向他和盤托出。他讓我了解基思的為人;說他完全沒有可能為我寫過任何信;認識他的人沒有一個對他有半點倚賴;對於省督給我信用狀的想法,他笑了,說他沒有信用可給。我表示擔心該怎麼辦,他勸我設法找一份自己行業的工作。他說:「在這裡的印刷商當中,你會進步,等你回美洲,就可以更有利地開業。」

passages.original: We both of us happen'd to know, as well as the stationer, that Riddlesden, the attorney, was a very knave. He had half ruin'd Miss Read's father by persuading him to be bound for him. By this letter it appear'd there was a secret scheme on foot to the prejudice of Hamilton (suppos'd to be then coming over with us); and that Keith was concerned in it with Riddlesden. Denham, who was a friend of Hamilton's thought he ought to be acquainted with it; so, when he arriv'd in England, which was soon after, partly from resentment and ill-will to Keith and Riddlesden, and partly from good-will to him, I waited on him, and gave him the letter. He thank'd me cordially, the information being of importance to him; and from that time he became my friend, greatly to my advantage afterwards on many occasions.
passages.vernacular: 我哋兩個同文具商一樣,都碰巧知道代書人里德斯登係個十足嘅無賴。佢勸里德小姐嘅爸爸替佢作保,幾乎令佢破產。從呢封信睇,有個針對漢密爾頓(當時以為同我哋一齊嚟緊)嘅秘密計劃,而基思同里德斯登有份。德納姆係漢密爾頓嘅朋友,覺得佢應該知道;所以佢到英國之後(不久之後),一半出於對基思同里德斯登嘅怨恨,一半出於對佢嘅善意,我就去拜訪佢,將信交畀佢。佢誠懇咁多謝我,因為呢個資訊對佢好重要;從嗰時起,佢成為我嘅朋友,之後好多場合都令我大大受益。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們兩個和文具商一樣,都碰巧知道代書人里德斯登是個十足的無賴。他勸里德小姐的父親替他作保,幾乎使他破產。從這封信看,有個針對漢密爾頓(當時以為和我們一起來的)的秘密計劃,而基思與里德斯登有份。德納姆是漢密爾頓的朋友,覺得他應該知道;所以他到英國之後(不久之後),一半出於對基思和里德斯登的怨恨,一半出於對他的善意,我就去拜訪他,把信交給他。他誠懇地感謝我,因為這個資訊對他很重要;從那時起,他成為我的朋友,之後許多場合都使我大大受益。

passages.original: But what shall we think of a governor's playing such pitiful tricks, and imposing so grossly on a poor ignorant boy! It was a habit he had acquired. He wish'd to please everybody; and, having little to give, he gave expectations. He was otherwise an ingenious, sensible man, a pretty good writer, and a good governor for the people, tho' not for his constituents, the proprietaries, whose instructions he sometimes disregarded. Several of our best laws were of his planning and passed during his administration.
passages.vernacular: 不過,我哋應該點睇一位省督玩出咁可憐嘅把戲,咁粗劣咁欺騙一個無知嘅窮男孩!呢係佢養成嘅習慣。佢希望取悅每個人;冇乜嘢可畀,就畀期望。除此之外,佢係個聰明明理嘅人,相當好嘅作家,對人民來講係個好省督,雖然對佢嘅委託人業主唔係,因為佢有時唔理業主嘅指示。我哋好幾條最好嘅法律係佢構思,並喺佢任內通過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,我們該怎麼看一位省督玩出這麼可憐的把戲,這麼粗劣地欺騙一個無知的窮男孩!這是他養成的習慣。他希望取悅每個人;沒有什麼可給,就給期望。除此之外,他是個聰明明理的人,相當好的作家,對人民來說是個好省督,雖然對他的委託人業主不是,因為他有時不理業主的指示。我們好幾條最好的法律是他構思,並在他任內通過。

passages.original: Ralph and I were inseparable companions. We took lodgings together in Little Britain at three shillings and sixpence a week--as much as we could then afford. He found some relations, but they were poor, and unable to assist him. He now let me know his intentions of remaining in London, and that he never meant to return to Philadelphia. He had brought no money with him, the whole he could muster having been expended in paying his passage. I had fifteen pistoles; so he borrowed occasionally of me to subsist, while he was looking out for business. He first endeavored to get into the playhouse, believing himself qualify'd for an actor; but Wilkes, to whom he apply'd, advis'd him candidly not to think of that employment, as it was impossible he should succeed in it. Then he propos'd to Roberts, a publisher in Paternoster Row, to write for him a weekly paper like the Spectator, on certain conditions, which Roberts did not approve. Then he endeavored to get employment as a hackney writer, to copy for the stationers and lawyers about the Temple, but could find no vacancy.
passages.vernacular: 拉爾夫同我係形影不離嘅伴侶。我哋一齊喺小不列顛街租咗住處,每星期三先令六便士——當時我哋負擔得起嘅上限。佢搵到幾個親戚,不過佢哋窮,幫唔到佢。佢而家話畀我知,佢打算留喺倫敦,從來冇打算返費城。佢冇帶錢嚟,所有能夠湊到嘅都用咗付船費。我有十五個皮斯托爾金幣;所以佢搵工作期間,不時向我借錢維生。佢先努力想入戲院,相信自己有資格做演員;但係佢去求嘅威爾克斯坦白勸佢唔好諗呢份工作,因為佢不可能成功。然後佢向帕特諾斯特街一位出版商羅伯茨提議,按某些條件替佢寫一份類似《旁觀者》嘅週報,羅伯茨唔贊成。然後佢努力想做僱傭作家,為聖殿一帶嘅文具商同律師抄寫,但搵唔到空缺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拉爾夫和我是形影不離的夥伴。我們一起在小不列顛街租了住處,每星期三先令六便士——當時我們負擔得起的上限。他找到幾個親戚,不過他們窮,幫不了他。他現在告訴我,他打算留在倫敦,從來沒打算回費城。他沒帶錢來,所有能夠湊到的都用來付船費了。我有十五個皮斯托爾金幣;所以他找工作期間,不時向我借錢維生。他先努力想進戲院,相信自己有資格做演員;但是他去求的威爾克斯坦白勸他不要想這份工作,因為他不可能成功。然後他向帕特諾斯特街一位出版商羅伯茨提議,按某些條件替他寫一份類似《旁觀者》的週報,羅伯茨不贊成。然後他努力想做僱傭作家,為聖殿一帶的文具商和律師抄寫,但找不到空缺。

passages.original: I immediately got into work at Palmer's, then a famous printing-house in Bartholomew Close, and here I continu'd near a year. I was pretty diligent, but spent with Ralph a good deal of my earnings in going to plays and other places of amusement. We had together consumed all my pistoles, and now just rubbed on from hand to mouth. He seem'd quite to forget his wife and child, and I, by degrees, my engagements with Miss Read, to whom I never wrote more than one letter, and that was to let her know I was not likely soon to return. This was another of the great errata of my life, which I should wish to correct if I were to live it over again. In fact, by our expenses, I was constantly kept unable to pay my passage.
passages.vernacular: 我即刻喺帕爾默度開工,佢係當時巴塞洛繆巷一間著名印刷所,我喺度做咗將近一年。我相當勤奮,不過同拉爾夫一齊,將我好大部分收入花喺睇戲同其他娛樂場所。我哋一齊用晒我所有皮斯托爾金幣,而家只係勉強度日。佢似乎完全忘記咗太太同孩子,而我就逐漸忘記咗同里德小姐嘅承諾;我只寫過一封信畀佢,仲係話畀佢知我唔似乎好快返去。呢個係我人生另一個大「勘誤」,如果可以重新活過,我希望改正。事實上,我嘅開支令我一直付唔起船費。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我立刻在帕爾默那裡開工,那是當時巴塞洛繆巷一間著名印刷所,我在那裡做了將近一年。我相當勤奮,不過和拉爾夫一起,把我很大部分收入花在看戲和其他娛樂場所。我們一起用完我所有皮斯托爾金幣,現在只是勉強度日。他似乎完全忘記了妻子和孩子,而我逐漸忘記了和里德小姐的承諾;我只寫過一封信給她,還是告訴她我似乎不會很快回去。這是我人生另一個大「勘誤」,如果可以重新活過,我希望改正。事實上,我的開支使我一直付不起船費。

passages.original: At Palmer's I was employed in composing for the second edition of Wollaston's "Religion of Nature." Some of his reasonings not appearing to me well founded, I wrote a little metaphysical piece in which I made remarks on them. It was entitled "A Dissertation on Liberty and Necessity, Pleasure and Pain." I inscribed it to my friend Ralph; I printed a small number. It occasion'd my being more consider'd by Mr. Palmer as a young man of some ingenuity, tho' he seriously expostulated with me upon the principles of my pamphlet, which to him appear'd abominable. My printing this pamphlet was another erratum. While I lodg'd in Little Britain, I made an acquaintance with one Wilcox, a bookseller, whose shop was at the next door. He had an immense collection of second-hand books. Circulating libraries were not then in use; but we agreed that, on certain reasonable terms, which I have now forgotten, I might take, read, and return any of his books. This I esteem'd a great advantage, and I made as much use of it as I could.
passages.vernacular: 我喺帕爾默度負責排沃拉斯頓《自然宗教》嘅第二版。佢有啲推理我覺得根據不足,所以我寫咗篇小型形而上學文章,對佢哋提出評論。題目叫《論自由與必然、快樂與痛苦》。我將佢獻畀我朋友拉爾夫;我印咗少量。呢篇令帕爾默先生多咗留意我,視我為有啲才智嘅後生,雖然佢認真咁就我小冊子嘅原則同我理論,佢覺得可憎。我印呢本小冊子係另一個「勘誤」。我住喺小不列顛街嘅時候,認識咗一個書商威爾科克斯,佢舖頭就喺隔離。佢有大量二手書。當時未有流動圖書館;不過我哋同意,按某啲合理條件(我而家忘咗),我可以攞、睇、還佢任何一本書。我覺得呢點好有利,盡量善用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在帕爾默那裡負責排沃拉斯頓《自然宗教》的第二版。他有些推理我覺得根據不足,所以我寫了篇小型形而上學文章,對它們提出評論。題目叫《論自由與必然、快樂與痛苦》。我把它獻給我朋友拉爾夫;我印了少量。這篇使帕爾默先生多留意我,視我為有些才智的年輕人,雖然他認真地就我小冊子的原則與我理論,他覺得可憎。我印這本小冊子是另一個「勘誤」。我住在小不列顛街的時候,認識了一個書商威爾科克斯,他的店就在隔壁。他有大量二手書。當時還沒有流動圖書館;不過我們同意,按某些合理條件(我現在忘了),我可以拿、看、還他任何一本書。我覺得這一點很有利,盡量善用。

passages.original: My pamphlet by some means falling into the hands of one Lyons, a surgeon, author of a book entitled "The Infallibility of Human Judgment," it occasioned an acquaintance between us. He took great notice of me, called on me often to converse on those subjects, carried me to the Horns, a pale alehouse in ------ Lane, Cheapside, and introduced me to Dr. Mandeville, author of the "Fable of the Bees," who had a club there, of which he was the soul, being a most facetious, entertaining companion. Lyons, too, introduced me to Dr. Pemberton, at Batson's Coffee-house, who promis'd to give me an opportunity, some time or other, of seeing Sir Isaac Newton, of which I was extreamely desirous; but this never happened.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅小冊子透過某種方式落入一位外科醫生賴昂斯手上,佢係《人類判斷之絕對可靠》一書嘅作者,令我哋相識。佢好留意我,經常探我傾呢類話題,帶我去咗奇普賽德某巷嘅「號角」淡啤酒館,介紹我認識《蜜蜂的寓言》作者曼德維爾博士,佢喺嗰度有個俱樂部,佢係靈魂人物,係最風趣、最有趣嘅同伴。賴昂斯亦喺巴特森咖啡館介紹我認識彭伯頓博士,佢答應遲早畀機會我見牛頓爵士,我極之渴望,不過從來冇發生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的小冊子透過某種方式落入一位外科醫生賴昂斯手上,他是《人類判斷之絕對可靠》一書的作者,使我們相識。他很留意我,經常來找我談這類話題,帶我去了奇普賽德某巷的「號角」淡啤酒館,介紹我認識《蜜蜂的寓言》作者曼德維爾博士,他在那裡有個俱樂部,他是靈魂人物,是最風趣、最有趣的夥伴。賴昂斯也在巴特森咖啡館介紹我認識彭伯頓博士,他答應遲早給機會我見牛頓爵士,我極其渴望,不過從來沒發生。

passages.original: I had brought over a few curiosities, among which the principal was a purse made of the asbestos, which purifies by fire. Sir Hans Sloane heard of it, came to see me, and invited me to his house in Bloomsbury Square, where he show'd me all his curiosities, and persuaded me to let him add that to the number, for which he paid me handsomely.
passages.vernacular: 我帶咗少少珍品過嚟,當中最主要係一個用石棉做嘅錢包,可以用火淨化。漢斯·斯隆爵士聽聞,嚟睇我,邀請我去佢喺布盧姆茨伯里廣場嘅屋,畀我睇佢所有珍品,說服我讓佢將呢件加入收藏,並大方咁付錢畀我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我帶了一點珍品過來,其中最主要的是一個用石棉做的錢包,可以用火淨化。漢斯·斯隆爵士聽說,來看我,邀請我去他在布盧姆斯伯里廣場的家,給我看他所有珍品,說服我讓他把這件加入收藏,並大方地付錢給我。

passages.original: In our house there lodg'd a young woman, a milliner, who, I think, had a shop in the Cloisters. She had been genteelly bred, was sensible and lively, and of most pleasing conversation. Ralph read plays to her in the evenings, they grew intimate, she took another lodging, and he followed her. They liv'd together some time; but, he being still out of business, and her income not sufficient to maintain them with her child, he took a resolution of going from London, to try for a country school, which he thought himself well qualified to undertake, as he wrote an excellent hand, and was a master of arithmetic and accounts. This, however, he deemed a business below him, and confident of future better fortune, when he should be unwilling to have it known that he once was so meanly employed, he changed his name, and did me the honor to assume mine; for I soon after had a letter from him, acquainting me that he was settled in a small village (in Berkshire, I think it was, where he taught reading and writing to ten or a dozen boys, at sixpence each per week), recommending Mrs. T------ to my care, and desiring me to write to him, directing for Mr. Franklin, schoolmaster, at such a place.
passages.vernacular: 我哋屋入面住咗一個年輕女子,係個女帽商,我諗佢喺迴廊有間舖頭。佢受過優雅教養,明理又活潑,談話最討人歡喜。拉爾夫夜晚讀劇本畀佢聽,兩人變得親密,佢搬去另一個住處,拉爾夫跟住去。佢哋同住咗一段時間;不過佢仍然冇工作,而佢嘅收入又唔夠養佢哋兩個同佢個孩子,佢決定離開倫敦,去試搵鄉村學校教書,佢以為自己好勝任,因為佢寫得一手好字,精通算術同賬目。不過,佢覺得呢份工作低過自己,又對將來更好嘅運氣有信心,到時唔想人哋知道佢曾經做過咁卑微嘅工作,就改名,賞面用我嘅名;因為我不久後收到佢封信,話佢定居喺一條小村(我記得係伯克郡),教十幾個男孩讀寫,每人每星期六便士,將T太太託付畀我照顧,叫我寫信畀佢,地址寫「某某地方富蘭克林先生,校長」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們屋子裡住了一個年輕女子,是個女帽商,我想她在迴廊有間店。她受過優雅教養,明理又活潑,談話最討人歡喜。拉爾夫晚上讀劇本給她聽,兩人變得親密,她搬去另一個住處,拉爾夫跟著去。他們同住了一段時間;不過他仍然沒有工作,而她的收入又不夠養他們兩個和她的孩子,他決定離開倫敦,去試找鄉村學校教書,他以為自己很勝任,因為他寫得一手好字,精通算術和賬目。不過,他覺得這份工作低於自己,又對將來更好的運氣有信心,到時不想別人知道他曾經做過這樣卑微的工作,就改名,賞臉用了我的名字;因為我不久後收到他的信,說他定居在一條小村(我記得是伯克郡),教十幾個男孩讀寫,每人每星期六便士,把T太太託付給我照顧,叫我寫信給他,地址寫「某某地方富蘭克林先生,校長」。

passages.original: He continued to write frequently, sending me large specimens of an epic poem which he was then composing, and desiring my remarks and corrections. These I gave him from time to time, but endeavor'd rather to discourage his proceeding. One of Young's Satires was then just published. I copy'd and sent him a great part of it, which set in a strong light the folly of pursuing the Muses with any hope of advancement by them. All was in vain; sheets of the poem continued to come by every post. In the mean time, Mrs. T------, having on his account lost her friends and business, was often in distresses, and us'd to send for me, and borrow what I could spare to help her out of them. I grew fond of her company, and, being at that time under no religious restraint, and presuming upon my importance to her, I attempted familiarities (another erratum) which she repuls'd with a proper resentment, and acquainted him with my behaviour. This made a breach between us; and, when he returned again to London, he let me know he thought I had cancell'd all the obligations he had been under to me. So I found I was never to expect his repaying me what I lent to him, or advanc'd for him. This, however, was not then of much consequence, as he was totally unable; and in the loss of his friendship I found myself relieved from a burthen. I now began to think of getting a little money beforehand, and, expecting better work, I left Palmer's to work at Watts's, near Lincoln's Inn Fields, a still greater printing-house. Here I continued all the rest of my stay in London.
passages.vernacular: 佢繼續經常寫信,寄大段佢當時寫緊嘅史詩樣本畀我,要求我評論同修改。我不時畀佢,不過寧願勸佢唔好繼續。揚格嘅一篇諷刺詩當時啱啱出版。我抄咗大部分寄畀佢,當中清楚顯示,抱住靠繆斯晉升嘅希望是何等愚蠢。全部徒勞;詩稿每班郵車繼續到。同時,T太太因為佢而失去朋友同生意,經常陷入困境,會叫我去,借我騰得出嘅錢幫佢渡過。我開始鍾意佢嘅陪伴,而當時我冇受宗教約束,又自恃對佢重要,就試圖做出親暱舉動(另一個「勘誤」),佢以適當嘅憤怒拒絕,並將我嘅行為告訴佢。呢點令我哋之間出現裂痕;佢再返倫敦時,話畀我知佢覺得我已經取消咗佢對我嘅所有虧欠。所以我知道,我永遠不要期望佢還我借畀佢、墊付畀佢嘅錢。不過,呢點當時並不重要,因為佢完全無力償還;失去佢嘅友誼,我反而覺得卸下一個負擔。我而家開始諗預先儲少少錢,期望更好嘅工作,我離開帕爾默,去林肯法學院廣場附近嘅沃茨印刷所工作,嗰間更大。我喺倫敦餘下嘅時間都喺度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他繼續經常寫信,寄大段他當時正在寫的史詩樣本給我,要求我評論和修改。我不時給他,不過寧願勸他不要繼續。揚格的一篇諷刺詩當時剛剛出版。我抄了大部分寄給他,當中清楚顯示,抱著靠繆斯晉升的希望是何等愚蠢。全部徒勞;詩稿每班郵車繼續到。同時,T太太因為他而失去朋友和生意,經常陷入困境,會叫我去,借我騰得出的錢幫她渡過。我開始喜歡她的陪伴,而當時我沒受宗教約束,又自恃對她重要,就試圖做出親暱舉動(另一個「勘誤」),她以適當的憤怒拒絕,並把我的行為告訴他。這使我們之間出現裂痕;他再回倫敦時,告訴我他覺得我已經取消了他對我的所有虧欠。所以我知道,我永遠不要期望他還我借給他、墊付給他的錢。不過,這一點當時並不重要,因為他完全無力償還;失去他的友誼,我反而覺得卸下一個負擔。我現在開始想預先儲一點錢,期望更好的工作,我離開帕爾默,去林肯法學院廣場附近的沃茨印刷所工作,那間更大。我在倫敦餘下的時間都在這裡。

passages.original: At my first admission into this printing-house I took to working at press, imagining I felt a want of the bodily exercise I had been us'd to in America, where presswork is mix'd with composing. I drank only water; the other workmen, near fifty in number, were great guzzlers of beer. On occasion, I carried up and down stairs a large form of types in each hand, when others carried but one in both hands. They wondered to see, from this and several instances, that the Water-American, as they called me, was stronger than themselves, who drank strong beer! We had an alehouse boy who attended always in the house to supply the workmen. My companion at the press drank every day a pint before breakfast, a pint at breakfast with his bread and cheese, a pint between breakfast and dinner, a pint at dinner, a pint in the afternoon about six o'clock, and another when he had done his day's work. I thought it a detestable custom; but it was necessary, he suppos'd, to drink strong beer, that he might be strong to labor. I endeavored to convince him that the bodily strength afforded by beer could only be in proportion to the grain or flour of the barley dissolved in the water of which it was made; that there was more flour in a pennyworth of bread; and therefore, if he would eat that with a pint of water, it would give him more strength than a quart of beer. He drank on, however, and had four or five shillings to pay out of his wages every Saturday night for that muddling liquor; an expense I was free from. And thus these poor devils keep themselves always under.
passages.vernacular: 我剛進呢間印刷所,就去做印刷機工作,想像自己覺得缺乏喺美洲習慣嘅體力活動,美洲嗰度印刷同排字係混合做嘅。我淨係飲水;其他工人近五十個,都係大量飲啤酒。有時,我兩隻手各拎一大版鉛字上落樓梯,其他人兩隻手先拎一版。佢哋見到,從呢件事同幾個例子睇,佢哋叫我做「飲水嘅美洲人」,居然比飲烈性啤酒嘅佢哋更有力,覺得好奇怪!我哋有一個酒館小廝,經常喺印刷所服侍工人。我喺印刷機嘅同伴,每日早餐前飲一品脫,早餐配麵包芝士飲一品脫,早餐同午餐之間一品脫,午餐一品脫,下午六點左右一品脫,收工後又一品脫。我覺得呢個習慣好討厭;不過佢以為必須飲烈性啤酒,先有力氣工作。我努力說服佢,啤酒提供嘅體力,只可能同溶入水中嘅大麥穀物或麵粉成比例;一便士麵包入面嘅麵粉更多;所以,如果佢食麵包配一品脫水,畀佢嘅力氣會多過一夸脫啤酒。不過佢繼續飲,每個星期六晚要從工資付四五先令買呢種令人迷糊嘅酒;呢筆開支我就冇。所以呢啲可憐人永遠都被壓住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我剛進這間印刷所,就去做印刷機工作,想像自己覺得缺乏在美洲習慣的體力活動,美洲那裡印刷和排字是混合做的。我只喝水;其他工人近五十個,都是大量喝啤酒。有時,我兩隻手各拿一大版鉛字上下樓梯,其他人兩隻手才拿一版。他們看到,從這件事和幾個例子看,他們叫我做「喝水的美洲人」,居然比喝烈性啤酒的他們更有力,覺得很奇怪!我們有一個酒館小廝,經常在印刷所服侍工人。我在印刷機的同伴,每天早餐前喝一品脫,早餐配麵包乳酪喝一品脫,早餐和午餐之間一品脫,午餐一品脫,下午六點左右一品脫,收工後又一品脫。我覺得這個習慣很討厭;不過他以為必須喝烈性啤酒,才有力氣工作。我努力說服他,啤酒提供的體力,只可能與溶入水中的大麥穀物或麵粉成比例;一便士麵包裡的麵粉更多;所以,如果他吃麵包配一品脫水,給他的力氣會多過一夸脫啤酒。不過他繼續喝,每個星期六晚要從工資付四五先令買這種令人迷糊的酒;這筆開支我就沒有。所以這些可憐人永遠都被壓著。

passages.original: Watts, after some weeks, desiring to have me in the composing-room, I left the pressmen; a new bien venu or sum for drink, being five shillings, was demanded of me by the compositors. I thought it an imposition, as I had paid below; the master thought so too, and forbad my paying it. I stood out two or three weeks, was accordingly considered as an excommunicate, and had so many little pieces of private mischief done me, by mixing my sorts, transposing my pages, breaking my matter, etc., etc., if I were ever so little out of the room, and all ascribed to the chappel ghost, which they said ever haunted those not regularly admitted, that, notwithstanding the master's protection, I found myself oblig'd to comply and pay the money, convinc'd of the folly of being on ill terms with those one is to live with continually.
passages.vernacular: 幾個星期後,沃茨想我去排字房,我離開印刷工;排字工人要求我交一筆新人酒錢「歡迎費」,五先令。我覺得係敲詐,因為我樓下已經付過;老闆亦咁認為,禁止我付。我堅持咗兩三個星期,於是被視為被逐出教會者,佢哋對我做咗好多私下嘅惡作劇,例如將我嘅鉛字混亂、將我嘅頁面調轉、打散我排好嘅版等等,我稍離房間就發生,全部歸咎於「工會幽靈」,佢哋話幽靈總係纏住未經正式接納嘅人,所以即使有老闆保護,我發覺自己都不得不屈服交錢,深信同要日日一齊生活嘅人關係惡劣係愚蠢嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幾個星期後,沃茨想我去排字房,我離開印刷工;排字工人要求我交一筆新人酒錢「歡迎費」,五先令。我覺得是敲詐,因為我樓下已經付過;老闆也這樣認為,禁止我付。我堅持了兩三個星期,於是被視為被逐出教會者,他們對我做了許多私下的惡作劇,例如把我的鉛字混亂、把我的頁面調轉、打散我排好的版等等,我稍離房間就發生,全部歸咎於「工會幽靈」,他們說幽靈總是纏著未經正式接納的人,所以即使有老闆保護,我發覺自己也不得不屈服交錢,深信與要天天一起生活的人關係惡劣是愚蠢的。

passages.original: I was now on a fair footing with them, and soon acquir'd considerable influence. I propos'd some reasonable alterations in their chappel laws, and carried them against all opposition. From my example, a great part of them left their muddling breakfast of beer, and bread, and cheese, finding they could with me be suppli'd from a neighboring house with a large porringer of hot water-gruel, sprinkled with pepper, crumbl'd with bread, and a bit of butter in it, for the price of a pint of beer, viz., three half-pence. This was a more comfortable as well as cheaper breakfast, and kept their heads clearer. Those who continued sotting with beer all day, were often, by not paying, out of credit at the alehouse, and us'd to make interest with me to get beer; their light, as they phrased it, being out. I watch'd the pay-table on Saturday night, and collected what I stood engag'd for them, having to pay sometimes near thirty shillings a week on their account. This, and my being esteem'd a pretty good riggite, that is, a jocular verbal satirist, supported my consequence in the society. My constant attendance (I never making a St. Monday) recommended me to the master; and my uncommon quickness at composing occasioned my being put upon all work of dispatch, which was generally better paid. So I went on now very agreeably.
passages.vernacular: 我而家同佢哋站穩腳跟,好快得到相當大嘅影響力。我提議對佢哋嘅工會規則作一啲合理修改,並克服所有反對通過。受我榜樣影響,佢哋好大部分人放棄令人迷糊嘅啤酒配麵包芝士早餐,發現同我一齊,可以喺附近一間屋攞到一大碗熱燕麥粥,撒胡椒、碎麵包同一小塊牛油,價錢同一品脫啤酒一樣,即係一個半便士。呢個早餐更舒服更便宜,頭腦亦更清醒。嗰啲繼續成日飲啤酒爛醉嘅人,經常因為唔付錢喺酒館冇信用,會央求我幫佢哋攞啤酒,用佢哋嘅講法,就係佢哋嘅「燈」熄咗。我星期六晚留意發薪桌,收返我為佢哋擔保嘅錢,有時為佢哋每個星期要付近三十先令。呢點,同我被視為相當好嘅「戲謔者」,即係開玩笑嘅口頭諷刺者,支持我喺社群中嘅地位。我不斷出勤(從不過「聖星期一」),令老闆欣賞我;而我排字特別快,令我被派去做所有趕急工作,通常薪酬更好。所以我而家過得好愜意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我現在與他們站穩腳跟,很快得到相當大的影響力。我提議對他們的工會規則作一些合理修改,並克服所有反對通過。受我榜樣影響,他們很大部分人放棄令人迷糊的啤酒配麵包乳酪早餐,發現和我一起,可以在附近一間屋拿到一大碗熱燕麥粥,撒胡椒、碎麵包和一小塊牛油,價錢和一品脫啤酒一樣,即一個半便士。這個早餐更舒服更便宜,頭腦也更清醒。那些繼續整天喝啤酒爛醉的人,經常因為不付錢在酒館沒信用,會央求我幫他們拿啤酒,用他們的說法,就是他們的「燈」熄了。我星期六晚留意發薪桌,收回我為他們擔保的錢,有時為他們每星期要付近三十先令。這一點,和我被視為相當好的「戲謔者」,即開玩笑的口頭諷刺者,支持我在社群中的地位。我不斷出勤(從不過「聖星期一」),使老闆欣賞我;而我排字特別快,使我被派去做所有趕急工作,通常薪酬更好。所以我現在過得很愜意。

passages.original: My lodging in Little Britain being too remote, I found another in Duke-street, opposite to the Romish Chapel. It was two pair of stairs backwards, at an Italian warehouse. A widow lady kept the house; she had a daughter, and a maid servant, and a journeyman who attended the warehouse, but lodg'd abroad. After sending to inquire my character at the house where I last lodg'd she agreed to take me in at the same rate, 3s. 6d. per week; cheaper, as she said, from the protection she expected in having a man lodge in the house. She was a widow, an elderly woman; had been bred a Protestant, being a clergyman's daughter, but was converted to the Catholic religion by her husband, whose memory she much revered; had lived much among people of distinction, and knew a thousand anecdotes of them as far back as the times of Charles the Second. She was lame in her knees with the gout, and, therefore, seldom stirred out of her room, so sometimes wanted company; and hers was so highly amusing to me, that I was sure to spend an evening with her whenever she desired it. Our supper was only half an anchovy each, on a very little strip of bread and butter, and half a pint of ale between us; but the entertainment was in her conversation. My always keeping good hours, and giving little trouble in the family, made her unwilling to part with me; so that, when I talk'd of a lodging I had heard of, nearer my business, for two shillings a week, which, intent as I now was on saving money, made some difference, she bid me not think of it, for she would abate me two shillings a week for the future; so I remained with her at one shilling and sixpence as long as I staid in London.
passages.vernacular: 我喺小不列顛街嘅住處太遠,我喺公爵街搵到另一個,對面係羅馬天主教小教堂。喺一間意大利貨倉嘅後面三樓。一位寡婦女士管理屋,佢有個女兒、一個女傭,同一個照顧貨倉但住喺外面嘅夥計。佢寄信去我上一個住處查詢我嘅品格之後,同意以同樣價錢每星期三先令六便士收留我;佢話更便宜,因為預期有個男人住喺屋可以提供保護。佢係寡婦,上咗年紀;曾經係新教徒,因為係牧師嘅女兒,不過被丈夫轉信天主教,佢好尊重丈夫嘅回憶;佢曾經同好多顯貴人士相處,知道一千個關於佢哋嘅軼事,可以追溯到查理二世嘅時代。佢膝蓋因為痛風跛咗,所以好少出房,有時需要陪伴;佢嘅陪伴對我好有趣,所以佢一叫我,我一定同佢過一個晚上。我哋嘅晚餐只係每人半條鯷魚,放喺一小條麵包牛油上,同兩個人半品脫麥酒;但樂趣在於佢嘅談話。我一直作息正常,冇畀屋入面添咩麻煩,令佢唔想我走;所以我提起聽講有個更近我工作嘅住處,每星期兩先令,我當時一心想儲錢,有啲差別,佢叫我唔好諗,因為佢以後每星期減我兩先令;於是我喺倫敦期間一直同佢住,每星期一先令六便士。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在小不列顛街的住處太遠,我在公爵街找到另一個,對面是羅馬天主教小教堂。在一間意大利貨倉的後面三樓。一位寡婦女士管理屋子,她有個女兒、一個女傭,和一個照顧貨倉但住在外面的夥計。她寄信去我上一個住處查詢我的品格之後,同意以同樣價錢每星期三先令六便士收留我;她說更便宜,因為預期有個男人住在屋裡可以提供保護。她是寡婦,上了年紀;曾經是新教徒,因為是牧師的女兒,不過被丈夫轉信天主教,她很尊重丈夫的回憶;她曾經與許多顯貴人士相處,知道一千個關於他們的軼事,可以追溯到查理二世的時代。她膝蓋因為痛風瘸了,所以很少出房,有時需要陪伴;她的陪伴對我很有趣,所以她一叫我,我一定和她過一個晚上。我們的晚餐只是每人半條鯷魚,放在一小條麵包牛油上,和兩人半品脫麥酒;但樂趣在於她的談話。我一直作息正常,沒給家裡添什麼麻煩,使她不想我走;所以我提起聽說有個更近我工作的住處,每星期兩先令,我當時一心想存錢,有些差別,她叫我不要想,因為她以後每星期減我兩先令;於是我在倫敦期間一直與她同住,每星期一先令六便士。

chapters.title: Return to Philadelphia 重返費城

passages.original: In a garret of her house there lived a maiden lady of seventy, in the most retired manner, of whom my landlady gave me this account: that she was a Roman Catholic, had been sent abroad when young, and lodg'd in a nunnery with an intent of becoming a nun; but, the country not agreeing with her, she returned to England, where, there being no nunnery, she had vow'd to lead the life of a nun, as near as might be done in those circumstances. Accordingly, she had given all her estate to charitable uses, reserving only twelve pounds a year to live on, and out of this sum she still gave a great deal in charity, living herself on water-gruel only, and using no fire but to boil it. She had lived many years in that garret, being permitted to remain there gratis by successive Catholic tenants of the house below, as they deemed it a blessing to have her there. A priest visited her to confess her every day. "I have ask'd her," says my landlady, "how she, as she liv'd, could possibly find so much employment for a confessor?" "Oh," said she, "it is impossible to avoid vain thoughts." I was permitted once to visit her. She was chearful and polite, and convers'd pleasantly. The room was clean, but had no other furniture than a matras, a table with a crucifix and book, a stool which she gave me to sit on, and a picture over the chimney of Saint Veronica displaying her handkerchief, with the miraculous figure of Christ's bleeding face on it, which she explained to me with great seriousness. She look'd pale, but was never sick; and I give it as another instance on how small an income life and health may be supported.
passages.vernacular: 喺佢屋嘅閣樓住咗一位七十歲嘅老小姐,過住極隱居嘅生活;我嘅房東太太同我講過佢嘅事:佢係羅馬天主教徒,年輕時被送去國外,住入修道院打算做修女;但係嗰個國家同佢水土不服,佢返咗英國,英國冇修道院,佢就發誓喺嗰種環境下盡可能過修女嘅生活。於是佢將全部財產捐去做慈善,只保留每年十二鎊維生,而佢仍然從呢筆錢入面捐出好多,自己只食燕麥粥,除咗煮粥之外唔生火。佢喺嗰個閣樓住咗好多年,樓下歷任天主教租客都准佢免費住,覺得有佢喺度係一種福氣。每日有一位神父探佢,聽佢告解。房東太太講:「我問過佢:『你咁生活,點可能搵到咁多嘢畀告解神父聽?』」「噢,」佢講,「虛妄嘅念頭係避免唔到嘅。」我獲准探望過佢一次。佢開朗有禮,談吐愉快。房間乾淨,不過除咗一張床墊、一張放住十字架同書嘅枱、一張佢畀我坐嘅凳,同壁爐上面一幅聖維羅妮卡展示手帕嘅畫(手帕上有基督流血面容嘅神蹟圖像,佢好認真咁向我解釋)之外,冇其他傢俬。佢面色蒼白,但從未生病;我將佢當作另一個例子,說明生命同健康可以靠多麼少嘅收入維持。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在她屋子的閣樓裡住著一位七十歲的老小姐,過著極隱居的生活;我的房東太太對我講過她的事:她是羅馬天主教徒,年輕時被送去國外,住進修道院打算做修女;但是那個國家與她水土不服,她回了英國,英國沒有修道院,她就發誓在那種環境下盡可能過修女的生活。於是她把全部財產捐去做慈善,只保留每年十二鎊維生,而她仍然從這筆錢裡捐出很多,自己只吃燕麥粥,除了煮粥之外不生火。她在那個閣樓住了許多年,樓下歷任天主教租客都准她免費住,覺得有她在是一種福氣。每天有一位神父探望她,聽她告解。房東太太說:「我問過她:『你這樣生活,怎麼可能找到這麼多東西給告解神父聽?』」「噢,」她說,「虛妄的念頭是避免不了的。」我獲准探望過她一次。她開朗有禮,談吐愉快。房間乾淨,不過除了一張床墊、一張放著十字架和書的桌子、一張她給我坐的凳子,和壁爐上一幅聖維羅妮卡展示手帕的畫(手帕上有基督流血面容的神蹟圖像,她很認真地向我解釋)之外,沒有其他傢俱。她面色蒼白,但從未生病;我將她當作另一個例子,說明生命和健康可以靠多麼少的收入維持。

passages.original: At Watts's printing-house I contracted an acquaintance with an ingenious young man, one Wygate, who, having wealthy relations, had been better educated than most printers; was a tolerable Latinist, spoke French, and lov'd reading. I taught him and a friend of his to swim at twice going into the river, and they soon became good swimmers. They introduc'd me to some gentlemen from the country, who went to Chelsea by water to see the College and Don Saltero's curiosities. In our return, at the request of the company, whose curiosity Wygate had excited, I stripped and leaped into the river, and swam from near Chelsea to Blackfryar's, performing on the way many feats of activity, both upon and under water, that surpris'd and pleas'd those to whom they were novelties.
passages.vernacular: 喺沃茨印刷所,我認識咗一個聰明嘅後生威蓋特,佢有富有嘅親戚,受過比大部分印刷工更好嘅教育;拉丁文過得去,識講法文,鍾意讀書。我教佢同佢一個朋友游水,落河兩次就教識,佢哋好快變成好游水嘅人。佢哋介紹我認識幾位鄉下紳士,乘船去切爾西睇學院同唐·薩爾特羅嘅珍品。返程時,應同伴要求(威蓋特激起咗佢哋嘅好奇心),我脫衣跳入河,由切爾西附近游到黑衣修士橋,沿途做咗好多水面同水下嘅動作,令對佢哋嚟講新奇嘅人既驚訝又高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在沃茨印刷所,我認識了一個聰明的年輕人威蓋特,他有富有的親戚,受過比大部分印刷工更好的教育;拉丁文過得去,會說法文,喜歡讀書。我教他和他一個朋友游泳,下河兩次就教會,他們很快成為很會游泳的人。他們介紹我認識幾位鄉下紳士,乘船去切爾西看學院和唐·薩爾特羅的珍品。返程時,應同伴要求(威蓋特激起了他們的好奇心),我脫衣跳入河,從切爾西附近游到黑衣修士橋,沿途做了許多水面和水下的動作,使對他們來說新奇的人既驚訝又高興。

passages.original: I had from a child been ever delighted with this exercise, had studied and practis'd all Thevenot's motions and positions, added some of my own, aiming at the graceful and easy as well as the useful. All these I took this occasion of exhibiting to the company, and was much flatter'd by their admiration; and Wygate, who was desirous of becoming a master, grew more and more attach'd to me on that account, as well as from the similarity of our studies. He at length proposed to me travelling all over Europe together, supporting ourselves everywhere by working at our business. I was once inclined to it; but, mentioning it to my good friend Mr. Denham, with whom I often spent an hour when I had leisure, he dissuaded me from it, advising me to think only of returning to Pennsilvania, which he was now about to do.
